articles.title: Super League: Wigan Warriors storm to League Leaders' Shield success with win vs Catalans Dragons and remain on treble course
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors clinched Super League's top spot and the League Leaders' Shield after a final-round 50-12 victory over Catalans Dragons, meaning Matt Peet's side remain on course for a domestic treble.
articles.body:
Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran score as Wigan demolish Catalans to win League Leaders' Shield; Super League play-offs on September 18, live on Sky Sports, with Grand Final on October 3

Wigan Warriors clinched Super League's top spot and the League Leaders' Shield after a final-round 50-12 victory over Catalans Dragons, meaning Matt Peet's side remain on course for a domestic treble.

Having clinched Challenge Cup glory in May at Wembley with victory over Hull KR, Wigan lifted their second piece of silverware on Friday via a dominant home success over the Dragons.

Warriors scored nine tries through Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, the retiring Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley and Adam Keighran. Keighran also added 14 points off the kicking tee.

The only other side capable of claiming top spot and the League Leaders' Shield had been Leeds Rhinos, and owing to their far greater points difference, a victory over Hull FC would have been enough had Wigan slipped up, but Peet's side ensured that was never likely to happen. In any case, Leeds fell to a shock 18-12 home defeat to Hull on Friday.

Wigan will now seek to finish their season by clinching a treble with Super League Grand Final success at Old Trafford on October 3, having suffered final defeat last season to Hull KR. They and Leeds will have next week off as the play-offs begin, before contesting respective semi-finals at home on September 25 and 26.

articles.title: College Fantasy Football: Get ready for Week 2 with our primer
articles.summary: Get ready for Week 2 of the college fantasy football season with Eric Froton's primer!
articles.body:
College fantasy football analyst Eric Froton sets the table for Week 2 of the CFF season.

Freeman immediately established himself as DJ Lagway's preferred option in Baylor's 17-16 loss to Auburn, erupting for 12 receptions, 154 yards and a touchdown in his Bears debut. Freeman accounted for 45.6% of Lagway's 333 passing yards, while no other Bear caught more than five passes. Freeman repeatedly delivered in money situations with two third-down conversions and two fourth-down grabs on Baylor's final possession. His 5-yard touchdown with nine seconds remaining nearly forced overtime before Baylor failed on the ensuing 2-point conversion.

The Oklahoma State transfer entered the year well behind Louis Brown IV in CFF drafts, making this one of Week 1's most actionable usage developments. Baylor threw 54 times against Auburn, so that volume won't be replicated every week, but Freeman demonstrated that he's more than a gadget/slot complement in Jake Spavital's offense. Lagway repeatedly looked his way with the game hanging in the balance, which is considerably more meaningful than piling up receptions in garbage time. With Freeman rostered in only 4% of Yahoo leagues immediately following the game, he profiles as an aggressive waiver add whose target ceiling suddenly looks much higher than anticipated.

The true freshman announced his arrival by shredding Ohio for 122 yards and two touchdowns on 15 carries, while catching both of his targets for another 47 yards and a score. That's 169 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns on 17 touches, with Rule averaging 8.1 YPC and notably out-carrying fellow RB Mekhi Nelson, 15-to-10. His 122 rushing yards were Nebraska's first 100-yard performance by a freshman running back since 2004, earning Rule Big Ten Freshman of the Week honors.

Rule's performance is particularly intriguing because the coaching staff had been talking him up well before the opener, suggesting this wasn't simply a small-sample eruption. Ohio head coach John Houser said Rule ran more physically than expected, an important observation for a 215-pound back whose explosiveness was already evident on film. Rule still has to contend with Nelson and Isaiah Mozee in a crowded room, but 17 touches in his collegiate debut is a powerful CFF signal. Rule immediately goes from speculative freshman stash to one of the more compelling Power Four waiver additions of Week 1.

Few freshmen made a louder opening statement than Glasker, who turned four touches into three touchdowns during BYU's 63-7 destruction of Utah Tech. Glasker caught three passes for a team-high 65 yards and two touchdowns while adding a 9-yard rushing score, displaying the explosive open-field ability that propelled him up BYU's depth chart during camp. His 21.7 yards per reception and absurd 75% touchdown rate aren't sustainable, but the explosiveness absolutely translates.

The important CFF takeaway is that Glasker's emergence didn't come out of nowhere. WR coach Fesi Sitake said during camp that Glasker had worked his way into the first-team offense and openly wondered why more Power Four programs hadn't recruited him. Glasker reportedly ran a 4.42 40-yard dash as a prep prospect and believes he's now in the 4.3 range, giving BYU a vertical/YAC weapon that its reconstructed receiving corps badly needed.

Arizona represents a dramatically tougher test, but Glasker has already forced his way onto the CFF radar and could become one of Bear Bachmeier's highest-upside targets.

Howard's breakout against Marshall looks even better under the advanced-data microscope. He was targeted on a staggering 44.4% of his routes and generated 9.47 yards per route run, while his 16.6-yard aDOT shows Penn State wasn't simply feeding him manufactured underneath touches. On intermediate throws alone, Howard caught all three targets for 107 yards and a touchdown, earning a 99.0 PFF receiving grade on those opportunities.

Head coach Matt Campbell's postgame comments further reinforce the idea that Howard has earned a larger role. Campbell praised Howard for routinely being in the facility around 5:15 a.m. catching balls off the JUGS machine, adding that "the sky is the limit" after watching him capitalize on his opportunity. That's significant for a sophomore who caught only seven passes for 133 yards last season but flashed 19.1 yards per reception.

Howard's route participation needs to expand before he's treated as a weekly CFF starter, but the combination of downfield deployment, target rate and coach endorsement makes him a priority speculative add.

Brown looks ready to make the sophomore leap after torching Florida's opener for six receptions, 117 yards and a touchdown, while also taking his lone carry for 14 yards. Brown's 49-yard catch-and-run touchdown was particularly encouraging, as QB Aaron Philo recognized pressure, quickly got Brown the ball in space and let him manufacture the explosive play. After leading Florida with 40 receptions and 512 yards as a freshman without scoring a touchdown, Brown found paydirt on his seventh offensive snap of 2026.

Head coach Jon Sumrall called Brown an "unbelievable worker" and one of the best young leaders he's been around, while Philo's comments were equally relevant for CFF managers: get Brown the football in space and allow him to create. Florida lost three of its top four receivers from 2025 and returned only about 36% of last year's WR snaps, leaving a significant opportunity vacuum despite the additions around him. Brown already owned the strongest returning production profile, and Week 1 provided evidence that Florida intends to feature him rather than merely make him part of a broad rotation. He's trending toward legitimate weekly CFF relevance.

Fletcher's final line wasn't disastrous, but his usage in Miami's 45-6 demolition of Stanford was disappointing relative to the game environment. Fletcher handled 13 carries for just 40 yards and caught both targets for 10 yards, finishing with 50 scrimmage yards and no touchdowns despite Miami producing six touchdowns. He still led the Hurricanes in rushing attempts, but Miami spread the backfield work around once the game got out of hand and generated only 121 rushing yards as a team.

There's no reason to panic about Fletcher's standing atop the depth chart, but this was precisely the type of matchup in which CFF managers expected a big rushing line and multiple scoring opportunities. Instead, Miami's passing game produced more than 400 yards and five touchdowns while Fletcher was largely left out of the fantasy bonanza. His workload should increase in competitive games, so this is more yellow flag than red, but Fletcher's ceiling becomes considerably shakier if Miami is comfortable emptying the bench in blowouts. He's a hold, though his Week 1 usage doesn't support treating him as an unquestioned high-end CFF RB1.

Dickey's concern isn't talent; it's the suddenly undeniable three-way committee in Lubbock. Dickey received 14 carries for 48 yards and caught two of three targets for 8 yards against Abilene Christian, but J'Koby Williams turned 13 attempts into 71 yards and a touchdown while Quinten Joyner received 10 carries for 43 yards and another score. Texas Tech therefore distributed 37 RB carries almost evenly among its top three backs.

That's an uncomfortable development for a player coming off 1,138 rushing yards and 14 rushing touchdowns on 211 carries in 2025. Dickey remains capable of explosive performances — his 263-yard eruption against Kansas last year is proof — but Williams is too dangerous to marginalize and a healthy Joyner gives the staff another legitimate Power Four back.

Dickey can remain fantasy relevant in Texas Tech's productive offense, but expecting another 200-carry season is difficult unless this rotation contracts. Until that happens, all three backs cannibalize one another's weekly CFF ceiling.

The Eric Morris era couldn't have started much worse offensively, with Oklahoma State generating only 10 points in a 24-10 loss to Tulsa. The Cowboys committed four turnovers, failed on three fourth downs and struggled to generate explosive plays, while LT Jacob Sexton's injury on the fifth offensive snap contributed to persistent pressure on QB Drew Mestemaker. The result was especially concerning because Mestemaker, RB Caleb Hawkins and WR Wyatt Young were supposed to bring schematic continuity from Morris' North Texas system.

Morris didn't sugarcoat it afterward, saying he was "utterly embarrassed" and acknowledging that an offense expected to be explosive "played awful." He also accepted responsibility as the play caller and said the staff needs to determine which players it can build around after an offseason in which Oklahoma State imported more than 90 newcomers.

That's the CFF problem: we don't yet know whether volume will concentrate around Mestemaker/Hawkins/Young or whether Morris will start shuffling personnel in search of answers. The system remains attractive, but until Oklahoma State proves it can efficiently sustain drives, every Cowboys skill player deserves a downgrade.

Lacy's highly anticipated 2026 debut was cut short when he suffered a leg bruise late in the third quarter of Ole Miss' 41-38 win over Louisville. Lacy had already handled 17 carries for 61 yards and a touchdown while catching four passes for 19 yards, putting him at 21 touches before leaving. He briefly returned for one play as a decoy before shutting it down, with Makhi Frazier assuming the primary backfield responsibilities afterward.

The encouraging news is that HC Pete Golding indicated Ole Miss escaped the Louisville game without serious injuries, reducing concern that Lacy is facing a lengthy absence. That's crucial for a player coming off 1,567 rushing yards and an SEC-record 24 rushing touchdowns in 2025, and his 21-touch workload through less than three quarters reinforces his elite CFF volume profile.

Frazier immediately becomes the backup to roster, but there's no reason yet to substantially downgrade Lacy absent a negative practice update. If active, he's still an upper-tier CFF RB1.

RBs Quaid Carr and Jayden Limar, Washington

Washington's backfield was decimated in one afternoon, as Carr, the Huskies' starter, suffered a hand injury requiring surgery while Limar injured his elbow in Sunday's 24-10 win over Washington State. Carr exited after five carries for 28 yards, while Limar subsequently assumed the lead role and recorded a team-high 12 carries for 47 yards and a touchdown before going down himself. HC Jedd Fisch said neither back will be back "for a while," although he stopped short of declaring either injury season-ending.

That immediately elevates Trey Cooley and freshman Brian Bonner into one of the more interesting CFF backfield situations to monitor. Cooley received four carries against Washington State and Fisch specifically identified Cooley and Bonner as the players who will lead the RB room during Carr and Limar's absence.

QB Demond Williams Jr. complicates the rushing projection after leading Washington with 61 yards and a touchdown, but somebody still has to absorb the vacated RB touches. Cooley is the immediate waiver target, while Bonner is the higher-variance stash in deeper formats.

Scott entered 2026 positioned for a substantial role but was dinged up in NC State's opener against Virginia, leaving his status uncertain heading into Friday's matchup with Richmond. Scott managed only seven carries for 20 yards before the undisclosed issue became a concern, and the latest public injury designation still lists him as questionable. No definitive return timetable has been announced beyond the possibility of returning against Richmond.

That's frustrating for CFF managers who drafted Scott expecting him to build upon the upside he displayed in 2025, including a career-high 196-yard rushing performance against Georgia Tech. For now, this is a situation where availability matters more than trying to interpret the disappointing Week 1 stat line; seven carries isn't enough volume to make a meaningful judgment about his role. If Scott practices fully and is cleared, Richmond offers an obvious rebound opportunity, but managers should have an alternative ready until NC State provides something definitive.

Last year's Texas-Ohio State opener was a CFF wasteland, with the Buckeyes grinding out a 14-7 victory in a game that produced 21 combined points and 296 passing yards. QB Arch Manning completed 17 of 30 passes for 170 yards, one touchdown and an interception, while QB Julian Sayin was even more restrained at 13-of-20 passing for 126 yards and one score. WR Jeremiah Smith was held to six catches for 43 yards, while neither team produced a 100-yard rusher or receiver. Texas actually rushed for 166 yards but went 1-of-5 on fourth down and 0-for-2 in the red zone, while Ohio State managed only 77 rushing yards and 2.3 YPC. The combination of elite defensive personnel, conservative quarterback deployment and an inability to finish drives completely suppressed what would normally be premium CFF assets.

Manning and Sayin both have a full season under their belts and should be afforded greater freedom, so another 14-7 rock fight isn't the expectation. However, last year's game demonstrates how dramatically the CFF ceiling can collapse when these two defenses dictate terms. That makes Manning, Sayin and even Smith less automatic than their résumés suggest, while secondary options such as WRs Ryan Wingo and Devin McCuin carry considerable risk if possessions and explosive plays are again limited.

The talent says shootout potential, but last year's 21-point slog provides enough evidence to temper CFF projections across the board.

articles.title: Career turning point: “I loved the idea of staying home”: How Caitlin Clark’s decision to choose Iowa over Notre Dame changed her basketball career
articles.summary: International Sports News: Before Caitlin Clark became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball, she was a highly recruited teenager from West Des Moines, Iowa, facing a m.
articles.body: Before Caitlin Clark became one of the biggest names in women’s basketball, she was a highly recruited teenager from West Des Moines, Iowa, facing a major college decision. Notre Dame had the tradition and championships, while Iowa offered something more personal: home and the chance to help build something special.On Nov. 12, 2019, Clark committed to Iowa over Notre Dame and Iowa State. What looked like a major recruiting win for Lisa Bluder became much more than that. It became a career turning point, putting Clark on the path to becoming the NCAA’s all-time leading scorer and leading Iowa to two national championship games. ESPN later revealed just how close she came to choosing a different path.How Caitlin Clark nearly chose Notre Dame before changing her mind?Caitlin Clark’s recruitment was already unusual because some of the biggest programs in the country wanted her long before she reached college. ESPN reported in November 2019 that Clark was ranked No. 4 nationally in the 2020 recruiting class, making her the highest-ranked recruit in Iowa’s class at the time. Her final choices eventually came down to Iowa, Iowa State and Notre Dame.Notre Dame had an obvious advantage in the eyes of many people around Clark. The Fighting Irish had won the 2018 national championship under Muffet McGraw and returned to the national championship game in 2019. Clark had grown up watching Notre Dame and was particularly drawn to stars such as Skylar Diggins. ESPN’s Wright Thompson later reported that Clark’s family also wanted her to attend Notre Dame.“My family wanted me to go to Notre Dame,” Clark told ESPN. “At the end of the day they were like, you make the decision for yourself. But it’s NOTRE DAME! ‘Rudy’ was one of my favorite movies. How could you not pick Notre Dame?”The decision became even more complicated because Clark actually told McGraw that she intended to attend Notre Dame. ESPN reported that Clark called McGraw after deciding that Notre Dame was the “smart” choice. She then called Bluder to deliver the bad news while Bluder was attending a field hockey game.But the story did not end there. Clark continued to have doubts, and Iowa assistant Jan Jensen eventually reached out to see where her head was. Clark admitted that she had changed her mind. The next step was far more difficult because she had to call McGraw again and tell her she was no longer coming to Notre Dame.ESPN’s account of the recruitment showed just how emotional that moment was for Clark. She was only 17 years old, sitting in her bedroom and preparing to call one of the most respected coaches in women’s basketball. Eventually, she made the call and then contacted Bluder. Clark committed to Iowa, and the coaching staff celebrated immediately.The decision became official when Clark announced her Iowa commitment publicly. ESPN reported that she chose the Hawkeyes over Notre Dame and Iowa State, giving Bluder the highest-ranked recruit of her tenure at that point.Why Caitlin Clark’s decision to choose Iowa became the real career turning point?The importance of Caitlin Clark’s decision was not simply that she stayed close to home. It was that she chose a program where she believed she could help create something bigger.In her 2026 appearance on “Post Moves with Candace Parker and Aliyah Boston,” Clark explained the thinking behind the decision in greater detail. She said there was something about Notre Dame that ultimately did not feel right, even though she respected the program and its history.“I loved the idea of going to a school that obviously had been to the Final Four in 1992 or 1993,” Clark said during the podcast. She then explained why Iowa appealed to her so strongly: “I loved the idea of, like, staying home and, like, trying to take a place that meant a lot to me and, like, the state of Iowa to somewhere they hadn’t been in a really long time.”But staying home was only part of the reason. Clark later revealed that Bluder’s belief in her played a major role in the decision.“I think just her belief in me from Day 1 when I stepped on campus, like she gave me the keys to the offense, really the program and had always constant belief in what I could do and what I can help achieve,” Clark said, according to Basketball Network.Clark also had a clear goal from the beginning. She said that when she first committed to Iowa, she wanted to take the Hawkeyes to the Final Four. At the time, that sounded ambitious because Iowa had not reached the Final Four since 1993.“A lot of people were like that would never happen,” Clark recalled.That belief eventually became reality. Iowa reached the Final Four in Clark’s junior season and returned the following year, giving the program back-to-back Final Four appearances for the first time in its history.How Caitlin Clark turned the Iowa decision into a historic college career?Caitlin Clark did not need several years to prove that Iowa had landed a special player. She arrived in Iowa City in 2020 and quickly became the centerpiece of the Hawkeyes’ offense, eventually turning the program into a national attraction.During her four-year Iowa career, Clark averaged 28.4 points, 8.2 assists and 7.1 rebounds while playing in all 139 games. She led the Hawkeyes to their first national championship game in 2023 and returned them to the title game again in 2024.The biggest transformation came during those final two seasons. Iowa entered the 2022-23 season without a Final Four appearance since 1993. Clark then helped the Hawkeyes reach the national semifinals, where they stunned undefeated defending champion South Carolina before falling to LSU in the championship game.A year later, Iowa reached the title game again. This time, the Hawkeyes defeated LSU in the Elite Eight before losing to South Carolina in the championship game.Clark’s individual numbers eventually became almost impossible to separate from Iowa’s rise. She passed Pete Maravich to become the NCAA’s all-time leading scorer during the 2023-24 season, while the Hawkeyes became one of the biggest attractions in women’s college basketball.Yet Clark also changed as a player during those four years. She later admitted that trusting her teammates was something she had to learn.“I think that was like a process of learning over the course of my career, especially trusting my teammates,” Clark said. “I felt like I always had to do it all myself.”By her junior and senior seasons, she understood that the Hawkeyes were better when everyone around her had the freedom to flourish.“I think especially my junior and senior year, like, that was the reason why we were so good, is cuz my teammates flourished in their roles, but I also trusted them and they trusted me,” Clark added.That development helps explain why Bluder’s early belief in Clark was so important.None of that was guaranteed when Clark was sitting in her bedroom at 17, preparing to call McGraw and reverse her Notre Dame commitment.She could have chosen the established powerhouse. Instead, she chose the place where she believed she could build something.That decision eventually gave Clark four years in an Iowa program where she became the central figure, broke records and helped take the Hawkeyes to places they had not reached in decades.“I loved the idea of staying home,” Clark explained years later.For Clark, though, staying home became much bigger than geography. Iowa gave her the opportunity to play with the freedom and responsibility she wanted, while Bluder’s belief gave her the confidence to chase a goal that seemed unrealistic at the time.She did not know exactly how far that decision would take her. But she knew she wanted to build something in Iowa. Looking back at everything that followed, the choice to turn down Notre Dame and stay home stands out as one of the defining turning points of Caitlin Clark’s career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Christian McCaffrey's workload will worry many, but Kaelon Black's usage is what the 49ers and fantasy managers need
articles.summary: Matt Harmon explains why Christian McCaffrey's reduced workload is actually a good thing for the veteran RB this season.
articles.body:
I regret to inform you that I think San Francisco 49ers rookie running back Kaelon Black seeing the exact usage that we witnessed on Thursday night is smart and ideal for everyone involved.

There is no doubt that Christian McCaffrey has been a transformative player for the 49ers since he arrived midway through the 2022 NFL season. His ability to bring every rushing concept to the table, alignment versatility as a receiver and overall gravity as a player has brought the offense to life. You can feel how much Kyle Shanahan appreciates his mere presence. You can also feel his pure addiction to just smashing the McCaffrey button over and over, with a complete inability to resist playing him on nearly every snap.

It was never more apparent than last season, when McCaffrey had an abnormal workload for a running back in the modern era.

While McCaffrey was a fantasy monster once again thanks to his receiving profile, we can be honest that it clearly took a toll on him as a rusher. McCaffrey ranked 23rd among 33 running backs with over 150 carries in EPA per rush and 28th in yards after contact per rush. Just 8.7% of his carries went for 10-plus yards, 28th out of 33 backs. He was far from one of the most impactful or effective rushers last year, to be kind.

I will never get it out of my head that McCaffrey described the 2025 campaign as "the hardest year of his life." While it wasn't all about the workload or even football, it was still a strenuous season on his body. It would make all the sense in the world for the team not to grind him into the dust on a weekly basis as he enters his age-30 season.

As a matter of fact, Shanahan even said himself back in May that it would be smart to not do so again.

It was fair to be skeptical that Shanahan would follow through on his statements, considering he's behaved as a man unable to resist the McCaffrey temptation in the past. That doesn't change the fact that it was a perfectly logical desire and even a sharp move.

I can also understand any skepticism over the idea that Shanahan and the 49ers would actually trust and use a rookie running back they took in the mid-rounds. Especially because Kaelon Black was a surprise Round 3 selection who some evaluators didn't even give a draftable grade. However, his on-field profile quietly fit the exact back they needed alongside McCaffrey. In my guy James Koh's charting of Black's college film, while he didn't find him to be an exciting playmaker whatsoever, he described him "as a viable, workmanlike back" and noted "when you go through the charting, all he does is give you positive plays."

Black looked like that exact player on Thursday night: finding holes in outside zone concepts, getting what was blocked to the tune of 14 carries for 65 yards. The 49ers have needed that exact back to be able to take the grinder carries away from McCaffrey. I remember doing shows with Austin Ekeler years ago and he was constantly pleading for the Chargers to find a back like that to pass off some of the work to stay fresh. There's no doubt McCaffrey wants the same at this stage of his career and Shanahan confirmed it was his desire as well.

To the point that it's good for McCaffrey, we referenced the 2025 rushing stats, or lack thereof, earlier. In Week 1, McCaffrey took 20% of his carries for 10-plus yards and averaged 6.8 yards per carry. He looked noticeably more explosive and ran with more aggression on fewer opportunities. McCaffrey also maintained a clear lead in the passing game with 18 routes and a team-high eight targets to 10 and one for Black.

McCaffrey might not have the absolutely legendary fantasy upside we've seen in his league-winner years if this split continues — which it should. Yet, the risk of injuries and a decline in rushing efficiency are much lower as a result. I don't know about you, but I want McCaffrey here for a long time this season, not just a good time early in the year. I'll take the trade-off.

From a brass-tacks perspective, the end results here aren't even bad in fantasy. Are you going to turn your nose up at 18 opportunities and 88 yards from scrimmage? I don't think so. People already have way bigger problems with some other fantasy players and we're not even out of the opening slate. This development won't come close to one of the things I'm panicking about most from Week 1.

If we redrafted today, McCaffrey would still be a fringe Round 1 selection for me. With games against the Dolphins and Cardinals on deck the next two weeks, I can't see myself ranking him outside of the top-five running backs.

Meanwhile, Black becomes one of the best running back stashes and backup insurance policy holds in the game with perhaps some level of standalone value. By the way, to speak to the foreseeable nature of where we are, this was true before Week 1. I added him to the end of my top-150 rankings this draft season after he enjoyed a strong preseason and earned the RB2 gig. Either way, Black should be one of the most-added players heading into Week 2.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 1 lineup picks
articles.summary: Looking for help setting your Week 1 fantasy football lineups? Justin Boone is here for you.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 1 rankings .

Despite being drafted outside the top-12 fantasy quarterbacks this year, Goff finds himself comfortably in the QB1 ranks for the season opener.

Last year's QB12 in fantasy points per game gets to begin his 2026 campaign at home in the domed environment of Ford Field, where he's statistically done his best work. In the last four years, he's averaged over 5.0 points per game more at home than on the road.

His Week 1 battle with the Saints features two of the fastest attacks in the league, with New Orleans finishing first in neutral offensive pace last season and the Lions ending up 12th. So, it should be no surprise that the Lions have the second-highest projected team total on the week.

Goff won't always be a strong fantasy start, but he's a mid-range QB1 in this matchup.

Justin Herbert vs. Cardinals – The only team with a higher projected point total this week is the Chargers. With Mike McDaniel calling plays for the Bolts and his two star tackles healthy, you can expect Herbert to be highlighted as a start more often this season.

Kyler Murray vs. Packers – Green Bay 's defense will be without Micah Parsons in the opening weeks, giving Murray and the Vikings a softer opponent to deal with. Though he flamed out in Arizona last year, Murray was a top-12 fantasy QB on a per-game basis in each of his six campaigns before that. Get ready for a bounce-back season in Kevin O'Connell's offense.

After missing time with a hyperextended knee in recent weeks, Kyle Monangai avoided the injury report and is set to suit up on Sunday. While that might concern some fantasy managers hoping to get the most out of Swift in Week 1, let me calm those fears.

When Monangai's playing time increased last season, Swift's numbers actually improved in fantasy. The veteran was the RB10 from Week 6 on, with Monangai offering RB26 production during that span.

Ben Johnson is pushing for his team to challenge the single-season points record, which is possible given the talent across Chicago 's offense. That quest will start by running up the score on the Panthers, who allowed the seventh-most fantasy points to RBs a year ago.

Even with Carolina's additions this offseason, it is no match for the Bears. Swift is a must-start RB2 with RB1 upside until further notice.

David Montgomery vs. Bills – We're about to learn how quickly Buffalo's defense can change under Jim Leonhard . While the long-term outlook is hopeful, it might take time for this unit to gel. For now, I'm still attacking this unit with RBs, after they gave up the sixth-most fantasy points to the position in 2025.

Jaylen Warren/Rico Dowdle vs. Falcons – The Falcons' defensive line is one of the worst in the league, which might be a problem against a team that wants to operate their offense through its running backs. The uncertainty at quarterback for Atlanta should also give the Steelers plenty of good field position and scoring opportunities. You can confidently start both Pittsburgh RBs in this game.

MarShawn Lloyd at Vikings – As we wait for the Josh Jacobs situation to play out , Lloyd will get the first opportunity to replace him as the starter. Brian Flores' defense always puts up a good fight, but this is a much different defensive line than the Vikings had last year and the impact could be felt in their run defense. Even though we'll likely see a committee approach for Green Bay's RBs, Lloyd is the most explosive playmaker of the group.

McMillan is coming off a solid rookie campaign where he put up 70 catches, 1,014 yards and seven touchdowns en route to being the WR22 in fppg for half-PPR scoring. Questions about Bryce Young 's ability are still unanswered, but McMillan is poised for another quality season-long stat line in 2026.

The first step in that journey starts at home against a banged-up Bears secondary that will be without cornerback Kyler Gordon and safety Coby Bryant . They even added safety Xavier Woods to the injury report on Thursday with a limited practice due to a groin issue.

If you weren't excited about McMillan's potential in Week 1 before this wave of injuries to Chicago's defense, you should be now. I have him ranked as a top-15 fantasy WR this week.

Ladd McConkey vs. Cardinals – McConkey is the No. 1 receiver in an ascending offense that's being projected to score the most points in Week 1. Don't overthink this situation, he's an excellent fantasy play against Arizona.

Jameson Williams vs. Saints – Last year's WR18 in fppg should pick up where he left off in a projected high-scoring matchup with the Saints on the fast track in Detroit . Bottom line, start your Lions players in this game.

Parker Washington vs. Browns – When his playing time increased, Washington was the WR19 in fppg over the final nine weeks of the fantasy season, posting 90 yards and/or a touchdown in five of his last seven outings. He should also avoid the tougher coverage in this contest, with Brian Thomas Jr. likely dealing with Denzel Ward on the outside.

Mayer was a late riser in the Week 1 rankings after news broke that Brock Bowers will miss a week or two following a meniscus trim. Though Mayer's mostly been relegated to serving as an overqualified No. 2 tight end behind Bowers in recent years, he has flashed TE1 upside in his limited starts.

In the four games where Bowers was sidelined last season, Mayer averaged 4.5 receptions and 49 yards per contest while finishing as a top-five fantasy TE in two of those outings.

This week, he'll get the benefit of facing a weak Dolphins defense that allowed the third-most fantasy points to tight ends last year.

If you're trying to find a replacement for Bowers or you're just unhappy with your current starting tight end, Mayer is in play as a viable starter with a very high ceiling this week.

Dallas Goedert vs. Commanders – As the Eagles get comfortable in OC Sean Mannion's new scheme and work new receivers like Makai Lemon and Dontayvion Wicks into the offense, I expect Goedert to serve as the No. 2 pass-catcher behind DeVonta Smith . Washington has made an effort to improve its defense, but this is a unit that gave up the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends in 2025.

Juwan Johnson at Lions – Johnson was the TE14 in fantasy points per game last year, with nine top-10 weekly finishes. Now that rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson is sidelined for the first month or more, Johnson is back in the mix as a low-end fantasy TE1.

For as long as he's in the NFL, Mahomes will always be in the conversation as one of the league's best quarterbacks. However, fantasy is a different competition.

Mahomes posted the fourth-most fantasy points per game last year, after a couple down seasons where he finished as the QB11 (2024) and QB12 (2023). His bounce-back occurred due to career-highs on the ground with 422 rushing yards and five touchdowns. It's unlikely he'll repeat those kind of stats in the first season after a torn ACL suffered in Week 15. Other quarterbacks returning from ACL tears have been hesitant to use their legs the following year.

With fewer rushing attempts and so many good quarterbacks to choose from in fantasy, Mahomes is a tough sell in general. That's even more evident in Week 1, when he squares off with a Broncos team that's held him in check each of the past two seasons.

Bo Nix at Chiefs – I also have concerns about Nix's outlook on the road in a tough environment in Kansas City . In a game with one of the lower projected totals on the week (43.5 points), you should look elsewhere for a fantasy starter.

Jordan Love at Vikings – Love has finished outside the top-20 fantasy QBs in each of his past two encounters with Brian Flores' defense. Better fantasy days are coming, but I wouldn't tempt fate by starting him here.

The Browns' rushing attack is running into a buzzsaw in Week 1. Jacksonville has one of the toughest defensive fronts in the league and were the third-stingiest opponent for fantasy RBs in 2025. According to the Jags' beat writers, things haven't changed and this group is ready to shut down ground attacks once again.

Judkins performed well in adverse conditions last season and could see his role grow on passing downs this year. However, in addition to the bad matchup, he also has to overcome uncertainty at quarterback.

In a game where the Browns are 8-point underdogs on the road, the degree of difficulty is just too high for Judkins to be trusted as anything more than a risky RB3/flex.

J.K. Dobbins at Chiefs – I'm taking a cautious approach to Dobbins in fantasy, until we know how the Broncos plan to deploy their three backs. RJ Harvey will resume his pass-catcher-plus role, but Jonah Coleman is the wild card. Based on how Sean Payton has raved about the rookie, it stands to reason that Coleman will be involved — which limits Dobbins' ceiling.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt at Eagles – This was already going to be a tough spot for the Commanders' rushing attack before they lost star tackle Laremy Tunsil . Leave JCM on your bench until we get a better matchup.

Aaron Jones Sr. vs. Packers – Jones was held under 10 fantasy points in five of last seven games and didn't top 15 points in any of his last 10 outings. He also came away with just 57 scoreless yards in his last meeting with the Packers. Entering his age-32 season, Jones is just a volatile flex play.

Moore will be a reliable addition for Josh Allen in a Bills offense that projects to throw more with Joe Brady taking over as head coach. Unfortunately, their Week 1 draw does Moore no favors.

The Texans were the second-worst opponent for fantasy wideouts last season and might be an even tougher challenge for opposing offenses in 2026. Houston also held Allen to one of his lowest outputs last year with 253 passing yards, 20 rushing yards, two interceptions and no touchdowns. If Moore has any hope to hit for fantasy this week, it would require taking advantage of broken plays.

Don't let a slow start discourage you from Moore's potential in Buffalo, though. This is still a player who's just one year removed from back-to-back campaigns with 96 catches and 98 catches. He's the best receiver Allen has had since Stefon Diggs .

Brian Thomas Jr. vs. Browns – Thomas still has to prove himself after a disappointing season in Liam Coen's first year in Jacksonville. Sadly, he'll face the strength of the Browns' defense at outside corner, making him a riskier WR3/flex play.

Courtland Sutton at Chiefs – Sutton was held under 60 yards in both matchups with Steve Spagnuolo's defense last year and failed to score a touchdown in either contest. Now, he'll also have to battle for targets with new No. 1 wideout Jaylen Waddle and promising sophomore Pat Bryant.

Alec Pierce vs. Ravens – Pierce is expected to play in Week 1, but he's spent all summer working his way back from an ankle injury. Even if he's active, you should avoid starting him at less than 100% against a feisty Ravens defense.

Finding a notable tight end to highlight in the Sit section is always tricky, since we know that a single touchdown can often vault a player into the low-end TE1 range — making it a very volatile position for fantasy.

Ferguson was a fantasy darling early last year, when he scored the most points among tight ends over the first seven weeks, while CeeDee Lamb was dealing with an injury and missed time. Once the Cowboys were healthy, Ferguson was the TE27 over the final 10 games of the fantasy season.

With Lamb, George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy ready to roll in Week 1, Ferguson becomes a touchdown-or-bust fantasy TE2. This one is less about the matchup and more of a concern for Ferguson's volume in the offense all season.

Dalton Schultz vs. Bills – Buffalo is implementing a new scheme, so we can't carry over many of its metrics from 2025, but the Bills were the second-toughest matchup for fantasy tight ends. As the Texans acclimate to life without their No. 2 receiver Jayden Higgins , Schultz will be streamable in fantasy, but maybe not this week.

Chig Okonkwo at Eagles – The arrival of Stefon Diggs, the loss of Laremy Tunsil and a brutal matchup with an Eagles defense that allowed the fewest fantasy points to the position last year. That all boils down to Okonkwo being off the fantasy radar in Week 1.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: From Daniel Jones' health to the Jaguars' RB situation, here are the storylines that will define Week 1
articles.summary: Chris Allen takes you through the storylines he believes will define Week 1 for fantasy football in 2026.
articles.body:
My wife and I have been watching the new HBO series Lanterns when we've got time. First, it's an excellent show. Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre are the perfect pairing. Anyway, I went in with expectations of a traditional superhero show. Some banter, lots of constructs and action sequences serving as the shroud for a single plotline. Instead, since the first episode, the storylines have diverged. Each with its own mystery that has me looking for clues each weekend.

The last two days have set us up for a similar atmosphere of confusion. We've already had tectonic injuries and an off-field legal case that have destroyed months of preparation. And we haven't even gotten to our first full Sunday of action. So, to help put most of Week 1 in perspective before the real chaos hits, here are the storylines I'll be monitoring as we take our first step into the 2026 season.

To be clear, the subtext to my subtitle isn't to point a conspiratorial finger at the Colts. I'll leave that to DK Metcalf . Regardless, Daniel Jones' mobility has been more proof of concept than fact.

Theoretically, Indianapolis ' QB1 is as healthy as can be. Jones has been a full participant in practice. By all accounts, he's taken his full reps without any restrictions. But even the clip above highlights how different a practice can be versus live action. Not to mention sustaining the same level of play for at least the next four months. And with three skill players in the top 100, I don't need to remind you of how things looked without Jones under center.

(Ranks in) Yards per Drive: 1st (Jones Healthy), 25th (Jones Hurt or Out)

Other than the nostalgia of watching Philip Rivers throwing TDs in 2025 , nothing was holding our interest in this offense. Jonathan Taylor went from the RB2 in PPG to the RB16. We had to talk ourselves into starting the pass-catchers. As such, we'll be watching every Jones dropback with bated breath.

Some play-caller/QB pairings, like Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay, aren't fair. California may have another in the works.

Watching Justin Herbert uncork a deep ball is a marvel. And yet, he was sitting close to the middle of the pack in completion rate on downfield shots last year. But new OC Mike McDaniel was creating explosives out of kindling in Miami . Hence the excitement surrounding the two connecting in L.A. But the tendencies surrounding McDaniel's play-calling have us second-guessing who benefits the most from the coaching hire.

Neutral Dropbacks per Game (2022-2025): 28th

From Jerick McKinnon to Elijah Mitchell to Raheem Mostert to De'Von Achane, the RBs under McDaniel have seen success as rushers and receivers. But the intertwining of the run and pass game left the Dolphins in the bottom five for play volume. We're sacrificing opportunity for efficiency. So while we like highlight plays from Herbert, if it's just one of 20 attempts on the day, there may be some worry about his value to our fantasy teams.

Kyler Murray : (Short) King in the North

We had two QBs sign veteran-minimum contracts elsewhere after their first team released them. But just one has fantasy appeal.

The Kyler Murray comeback tour begins in Minnesota this Sunday. He'll have everything he needs. An above-average offensive line , one of the better play-callers and a top-tier supporting cast would be any QB's dream. Plus, looking back at Murray's last full season as a starter, there's reason to buy into the pieces connected to the passing game.

2024 Target Rate to Top Target Earner: 4th (among all starters)

I chose these stats specifically because you can almost see which receiver connects to each metric. Justin Jefferson has top-12 upside with a boost in target quality, while maintaining his WR1 role. Even Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson become speculative adds (especially with Brock Bowers shifting the TE landscape) with more stability under center. The distribution might adjust each week, but the down-to-down efficiency from Murray will be the top storyline for the Vikings in Week 1.

I usually don't pay much attention to depth charts. But I take notice when they hint at the confirmation of a prior that I've held most of the offseason.

I highlighted Bhayshul Tuten as one of the worst picks of the middle rounds . Nothing against him personally. But with little usage as a receiver (66th in route rate, 60th in target share – min. 200 snaps), he has a fragile workload. And the team signing Chris Rodriguez Jr., who plays a similar style and has ties to the HC, doesn't help Tuten's case to be the unquestioned RB1.

On the bright side, Jacksonville 's OC did indicate Tuten has tried to grow in all RB roles . And LeQuint Allen Jr., who analysts expected to take on the coveted third-down job , is dealing with an injury. The situation keeps hope alive for Tuten drafters, but how the rotation shakes out will alter their value by Tuesday.

Will Rico Dowdle Take Over Another Backfield?

I'm willing to be open to the idea that I've missed something regarding Rico Dowdle.

The former Panther finds himself on another committee with an established RB at the head. And after watching Aaron Rodgers prefer short passes to getting hit, the environment doesn't lend itself to Dowdle. Jaylen Warren has been the de facto receiving RB. But two things stand out to me.

Rushing Rate (Weeks 9-18): 67% (Dowdle), 29% (Hubbard)

Dowdle has already taken somebody else's job before. Chuba Hubbard was active and healthy over the back half of the year, but the former Cowboy was the RB1. And while Warren may have earned more targets, Dowdle was more effective with his receptions (1.21 vs 1.18 YPRR). In short, as HC Mike McCarthy suggested, the workloads may not be as defined as we think.

Plus, there's the offensive environment to consider. Pittsburgh made additions to its line. Brought in another receiver. The Steelers could look like a modern offense. In that situation, Dowdle profiles as the better option. Not Warren.

Players make all sorts of proclamations about their health. But when J.K. Dobbins made a claim about his sixth year in the league, my ears perked up.

A full season with a top-rusher accolade by Week 17 at an RB33 price? Name your terms. I'll accept any. But Dobbins' own history is working against him. He's missed no fewer than four games since joining the league. Plus, even when healthy, we had questions about the sustainability of his production.

Rushing Success Rate (2024, 2025): 21st (out of 41 qualifiers – min. 30% rushing rate)

In 2025, Dobbins' ceiling was RB14. Despite two games over the century mark and one score in four of 10 starts, the Broncos RB1 couldn't crack the top 12. Even worse, he couldn't garner more than two targets a game.

Dobbins' inability to seize all phases of the job is where RJ Harvey holds our interest. He ended the season as one of 10 rushers with a double-digit target share. And he mixed in as the two-minute option, early-down starter and pass protector. If a split, or even a debut from rookie Jonah Coleman , occurs in Week 1, Dobbins will only be able to keep part of his promise.

All Right, Joe Brady. Show Us What You Got

The Bills promoted their OC and brought on a WR that most fans of his previous team were happy to see him go. Admittedly, my framing paints a pessimistic picture. But there's more to be excited about with Buffalo coming into '26.

DJ Moore reunites with his play-caller from Carolina and walks into the WR1 role without much challenge. While Moore's days of operating as a primary X-receiver are (mostly) over, he shouldn't leave the field under Brady.

In obvious passing situations, the Bills ran the 14th-most plays with at least two TEs on the field. The Bears were just ahead of Buffalo, and Moore had the highest route rate of any Chicago WR and earned just one fewer target than Rome Odunze . Plus, with Keon Coleman or Josh Palmer likely taking the split-end reps, Moore should see more off coverage, allowing him to use his route-running ability to create separation. But back to those heavy-personnel packages I was mentioning.

Dalton Kincaid has been at practice without any setbacks to the lingering effects of the PCL and soft-tissue injuries that plagued him in 2025. And when healthy, he led all Bills' pass-catchers in TPRR. Buffalo is returning four of last year's five starting offensive linemen, giving Josh Allen and James Cook II the same runways. But with Brady taking on a larger role on the team, the story will be how the aerial attack flows through Moore and Kincaid.

Everyone remembers the growing pains that Bears fans had to experience during the first season of Caleb Williams with Ben Johnson. The Titans may be going through the same.

The early returns on Year 2 of Cam Ward have been, to be kind, mixed . He still tends to drift in pockets while waiting for routes to develop. His ball security, or lack thereof , will have fantasy managers gripping their seats any time he scrambles. The lag in synchronizing the offense has wreaked havoc on the outlook for Tennessee 's strongest receiving asset.

(Pre-Season) Air Yard Share: 1st (among TEN pass-catchers)

Looking back at last season, Brian Daboll's QBs ( Jaxson Dart , Russell Wilson ) were just above the league average in passing aDOT and average time to throw. Their use of quick hitters and pre-snap motion took some of the pressure off them. But in Tennessee, we're yet to see how Daboll will adjust his concepts to Ward's style. And without a strong debut against a weaker opponent, our hopes of scooping late-round value with the Titans may have been a bad strategy.

articles.title: Bold Fantasy Football Predictions for Week 1
articles.summary: Which one of these fantasy football predictions is most likely to come true?
articles.body:
The Yahoo Fantasy Football crew is ready to get bold for Week 1. Which one of these predictions will come true?

Chris Olave finishes as the overall WR1 in Week 1

I know the quarterback situation in New Orleans is going to make people nervous, but this matchup has all the ingredients for the Chris Olave show. Alvin Kamara looks questionable, first-round rookie Jordyn Tyson will not play and the Saints are facing what many expect to be the best offense in the NFL.

Detroit is going to score points. If New Orleans wants to keep up, Tyler Shough is going to have to throw the football and his easiest answer will be feeding Olave. Olave is coming off career highs with 100 catches, 1,163 yards and nine touchdowns on 155 targets. He finished as the WR7 in fantasy points per game and already showed us this exact ceiling with a 10-catch, 148-yard, two-touchdown performance last season.

I am calling for double-digit targets, more than 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns. There will be bigger names attached to better quarterbacks across the Week 1 slate, but very few receivers have a clearer path to dominating their team's passing volume. Olave takes advantage of the game environment and opens the season as the overall WR1. — Ray Garvin

Across 398 snaps where all three of Josh Downs, Tyler Warren and Alec Pierce were on the field together last year, Downs paced the trio with a 27% target share. He was the only one of the three to be targeted on over 20% of his routes. Being on the field has been the only limitation for Downs and that variable is no longer in the way, even with the arrival of Keenan Allen , who likely comes on the field as the Z receiver in 11 personnel.

Alec Pierce looks like he'll be available for Week 1 but it would be tough to imagine him getting a ton of consistent volume after missing almost all of the summer and facing the Ravens in Week 1. Jesse Minter put out some of the toughest zone coverages in the NFL the previous two seasons in Los Angeles , which will be tough for the vertical receiver to crack. I'm expecting to see a ton of targets pushed Downs' way from the slot in Week 1 and beyond. — Matt Harmon

Kyler Murray outscores fellow running QB Jayden Daniels

It hasn't always been pretty, but since 2022, Murray is the QB12 in fantasy points per game in the era where he wasn't an elite rushing QB coming off a torn ACL. This 2026 Vikings team is light years better than those Cardinals teams — from coaching, receivers, OL, ownership, down to cafeteria food.

Kevin O'Connell has turned Nick Mullens into a fantasy QB1 for a stretch and Kirk Cousins and Sam Darnold into QB1s for entire seasons. A matchup against the Packers without Micah Parsons in a new scheme is one to target, and the Vikings' No. 10 team total confirms that. Meanwhile, Washington is 28th in team total. Daniels will run maybe a little bit more, but it's not enough to overcome the environment Murray has in the opener at home in front of fans desperate for watchable QB play. — Hayden Winks

Jalen Coker outscores your opponents' FLEX

After coming back midseason in 2025, Jalen Coker ended the season with 90% of snaps played in the final two games. The last time we saw the young wideout he had 12 targets and nine receptions for 134 yards and a score, not to mention it was a playoff game versus the Rams. I believe that'll carry over to 2026 in Week 1 versus Chicago .

The Bears defense looks shaky with DBs Kyler Gordon and Coby Bryant both out of the lineup. They were last against slot WRs, where Coker and McMillan will split work this season. Since Week 13, Coker has out-targeted McMillan, and I wouldn't expect a huge target difference this week. McMillan is being ranked inside the top 15 in this nice matchup, while Coker is going unconsidered. — Joel Smyth

We've typecast the Lions' WRs: Amon-Ra St. Brown is the target hog who earns easy looks, while Jameson Williams runs downfield. One is an every-week starter. The other at least has FLEX appeal. But in his fourth season, the Lions gave Williams a chance to change his stripes. Over the final six weeks, his receiving aDOT fell by 25.8% to 11.8. With more screens and interior targets added to his diet, not only did Williams' catchable target rate soar (up to 81% from 70%), but so did his efficiency from a per-route perspective. He turned his big-play ability into down-to-down reliability.

But even better for Williams is his Week 1 matchup. New Orleans is returning their primary outside defenders from 2025. They're the same guys who tied for allowing the ninth-most yards per reception last year. This game already has high-scoring potential with the second-highest total on the week. While everybody looks to the Sun God, I'll be watching his teammate run by him with the ball into the end zone. — Chris Allen

The Brock Bowers ' injury news was a gut punch for fantasy managers this week. Fortunately, the next man up in the Raiders' tight end room has shown he can be a strong fantasy option when Bowers is sidelined. Mayer started four games last year, averaging 4.5 catches and 49 yards per contest while finishing as a top-five fantasy TE twice. His other two starts came against a Chiefs defense that was the seventh toughest matchup for his position.

This week Mayer gets the Dolphins, who were the third easiest opponent for tight ends and will be a defense to target in fantasy once again. Without a proven No. 1 receiver, Klint Kubiak's offense is projected to feature the tight end even with Bowers out, setting Mayer up for a busy afternoon. Don't hesitate to get the former second-round pick in your lineup this week and he might even stay there for a couple games until Bowers returns. — Justin Boone

Tight ends are too often overlooked as legit FLEX options. Juwan Johnson should immediately be in consideration to open the season. The TE3 in receiving yards last year finds himself as the Saints' second-best pass catcher for (at least) the opening six weeks while Jordyn Tyson is sidelined. He finished as a top 12 tight end in eight games last season, including Weeks 1 and 2. I will gladly take the 900 receiving yards again this year — the real boost needs to be in the touchdown department, to improve on the three scores in 2025. Playing 41% of his snaps in the slot on a team that will be one of the fastest paced offenses in the league will help. The Lions will also be without both starting safeties, Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph . — Josh Norris

Pollard is the exact opposite of a hipster pick, entering his age-29 season and tied to a poor Tennessee offensive line. And the entire offense might be swimming under water, given how bad Cam Ward looked all summer. But Pollard has found a way to survive before — he's been over 1,000 yards rushing four straight years, including two in Tennessee — and this week he takes aim at a New York front seven that was the biggest turnstile in the league last year . It's not often we can link to Pollard as a correlation play, but Tennessee is actually favored in the opener, so his workload should be safe. Dial him up aggressively. — Scott Pianowski

articles.title: Lindblad crashes as Antonelli fastest in Madrid
articles.summary: Arvid Lindblad crashes his Racing Bulls in Friday practice at the Spanish Grand Prix, where Kimi Antonelli sets the fastest time.
articles.body:
British rookie Arvid Lindblad crashed his Racing Bulls in Friday practice at the Spanish Grand Prix shortly after setting an impressive fourth fastest time.

The 19-year-old lost control into Turn 13, and slid sideways into the wall, damaging his front and rear suspension and breaking his front wing.

Lindblad ended the session fourth fastest, just 0.228 seconds behind pace-setter Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes in Madrid.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were second and third fastest, just over 0.1secs behind Antonelli.

Antonelli's team-mate George Russell, who trails the Italian by 66 points in the championship, was fifth fastest ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

World champion Lando Norris did not set a time in his McLaren because of a gearbox problem.

Lindblad's incident was the only one of the day in Formula 1 running, but it did back up some remarks from Russell before the first session that the new Madring track had "less margin than Monaco, purely because of the speed".

Russell added: "In Monaco, the walls are closer, but because you're going far slower, if you make a mistake, you're not into the wall as quickly, and you can recover it sometimes, a small lock-up.

"There's a lot of really fast corners, but the barrier is kind of like coming back on to the track. So, if you are to go wide and hit the wall, you're not hitting it kind of at the same angle as the car is going. The wall is sort of coming in at you."

Russell singled out Turns Five, Seven and 17, where Leclerc went off into the run-off area at Turn 17.

Russell said: "Another element of the challenge here, which probably won't cause major crashes, but I think there'll be a lot of lock-ups.

"You've got three corners where you're turning and braking, and if you lock up, the wall is right in front of you, which is very reminiscent of the corner in Baku, Turn 15. You know, the one down the hill where a lot of people go off."

There is also a section of high-speed swerves, Russell said, which is similar to the fast Jeddah street track in Saudi Arabia.

articles.title: Borussia Dortmund’s Konstantinos Karetsas discharged from hospital, yet still out for Paderborn
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund will be without Konstantinos Karetsas for Saturday’s Bundesliga home fixture against SC Paderborn as further examinations continue followin...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund will be without Konstantinos Karetsas for Saturday's Bundesliga home fixture against SC Paderborn as further examinations continue following the 18-year-old's worrying withdrawal from Tuesday's Champions League victory over Villarreal . Karetsas has since been released from hospital after suffering circulatory problems during Dortmund's 3-2 win at the Westfalenstadion.

The Greek international did not participate in team training on Thursday and will not be available for the weekend. Dortmund sporting director Ole Book has now confirmed that initial examinations have yet to establish a specific cause.

"He is doing as well as can be expected under the circumstances," Book told the local Ruhr Nachrichten newspaper. "Further examinations are ongoing. We want to get to the bottom of this properly. The prognosis will then depend on that."

Book emphasized that Karetsas' health remains the club's overriding concern.

While Karetsas' mother Irena Kitsinis told Belgian newspaper Het Nieuwsblad that the episode appeared to have been related to dehydration, Dortmund have not yet established a definitive explanation for the problem.

The youngster has consequently been ruled out of the Paderborn fixture, with no timetable currently available for his return.

Dortmund remain cautious over Karetsas return

Karetsas' withdrawal against Villarreal caused considerable concern among his teammates and club officials. The summer signing sat down on the pitch during the first half before eventually being carried off on a stretcher. Dortmund subsequently confirmed that he had complained of circulatory problems before being transported to hospital.

Managing director Lars Ricken later praised the squad's response to seeing a teammate leave the pitch under uncertain circumstances, while Book acknowledged immediately after the match that the incident had caused concern throughout the club.

Karetsas has since been discharged, providing Dortmund with some positive news, but the club have made clear that no return will be contemplated until the cause of the episode has been properly investigated.

Head coach Niko Kovac confirmed ahead of Saturday's match that Karetsas will not feature against Paderborn.

His absence further reduces Dortmund's options in the advanced midfield positions after fellow Greek international Giannis Konstantelias suffered a major ACL tear in the opening Bundesliga victory over Hamburger SV .

Ethan Nwaneri , who replaced Karetsas against Villarreal, impressed after coming on and represents one of the alternatives available to Kovac this weekend.

articles.title: Drew Brees thinks Bears Caleb Williams is closer to a breakthrough than you think
articles.summary: Count Drew Brees among those who see big things on the horizon for the Bears QB1, Caleb Williams. @kdthompson5 has the details here.
articles.body:
For all Caleb Williams ' brilliance in his third season with the Chicago Bears , the burgeoning star quarterback can still get that much better as a passer—a frightening prospect for the NFL, if you ask me.

In particular, Williams' 58.1% completion percentage, a year after completing just 62.5% of his passes as a rookie, is due for an improvement in Year 3, which will mark his second under Ben Johnson.

But for those worried about whether Williams can make meaningful strides in that area, Hall-of-Fame quarterback Drew Brees had some advice for Williams that might put things in perspective.

Brees, who is now working as a color analyst for FOX Sports alongside Adam Amin, recently spoke with Williams as part of their preparations for the Bears' season-opening contest against the Carolina Panthers . Amin shared an especially interesting piece of that conversation on 104.3 The Score yesterday . (Also, don't forget to check out Adam's chat with our own Bill Zimmerman when you're done reading this.)

"Drew's line at the end of our conversation with Caleb—he said, 'You know what the difference is between a 60% passer and a 70% passer?' Caleb's answer was—he was hesitant, but he goes, 'Is it checkdowns?'

"Drew's answer was 'Three completions.'" You get three more completions per game when you're probably going to throw the ball 30 times per game."

First of all, Williams getting to speak with one of the greatest quarterbacks to ever do it—a man who completed almost 68% of his career pass attempts—is absolutely invaluable.

Secondly, what a way to put the task at hand in plain but attainable terms.

When you take away the league-leading 40 throwaways Williams made last year—another underrated sign of his growth—you could generally point to two or three passes a game where the ball simply got away from the young quarterback, who had the third-highest "bad-throw" percentage among all quarterbacks according to Pro Football Reference. (Plus, let's not forget he also suffered from the fourth-highest drop rate from his pass catchers at 5.5%. He also had 18 balls batted at the line of scrimmage, second-most in the NFL.)

The good news, Amin said, is that these improvements are a matter of smaller adjustments and fundamental tweaks than wholesale overhauls.

"A few adjustments here and there are all it's going to take to get small plays that lead to extended drives that lead to four extra points instead of having to settle for a field goal. These are the little things that build up and compound over time, and that's a good entry point to be in Year 2 in an offense," the broadcaster said.

A little bit of positive regression in each of these stats, and it wouldn't be hard to see Williams' completion rate jump into the mid-60s, even as he continues to big-game hunt and generate explosive plays.

We might be talking about an MVP-caliber player sooner rather than later.

And all it might take, at least to start with, is three more completions a game. Imagine that.

articles.title: Athletic Club forward Williams retires from Ghana duty
articles.summary: Inaki Williams says the time has come to bring his journey with the Black Stars to an end four years after making his international debut.
articles.body:
Athletic Club forward Inaki Williams has announced his retirement from international duty with Ghana .

The 32-year-old scored two goals in 28 caps for the Black Stars after making his debut in September 2022.

He featured for the West Africans at the 2022 and 2026 Fifa World Cups and the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon).

Williams appeared twice at this year's World Cup as Ghana were knocked out in the last 32 by Colombia .

"I feel the time has come to bring my journey with the Ghana national team to an end," he said in a post on social media.

"I leave happy, proud and with the peace of mind of knowing that I gave everything every time I wore this shirt."

Williams, who was born in Bilbao to Ghanaian parents, chose to represent the Black Stars after previously playing for Spain at youth level and in a 2016 friendly at senior level.

His younger brother Nico, who also plays for Athletic Club in Bilbao, chose to represent Spain and has gone on to become a World Cup and European Championship winner with La Roja.

Inaki Williams' announcement comes a week after it was confirmed that Carlos Queiroz would return as Ghana coach in the build-up to the 2027 Afcon in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

He said his time with Ghana had given him "much more than football".

"It has allowed me to come back home, feel even closer to my roots and experience the enormous pride of representing my country and wearing this flag on my chest," he added.

"Thank you from the bottom of my heart to everyone who has been part of this journey and for all the love you have always shown me.

"Ghana will always be a part of me. I will continue supporting the Black Stars as one of you, wherever I am."

articles.title: Rudy Gobert Gets A Major Respect Nod From Nikola Jokic
articles.summary: Rudy Gobert has spent years dealing with mixed reviews about his defense. That debate looks different when one of the NBA’s best offensive players gives him...
articles.body:
Rudy Gobert has spent years dealing with mixed reviews about his defense. That debate looks different when one of the NBA's best offensive players gives him credit for making the game harder.

Nikola Jokic has faced Gobert plenty of times and knows where the Timberwolves center can cause problems. His latest comments give Gobert a notable endorsement from someone who has spent years trying to attack him.

Rudy Gobert Earned Nikola Jokic's Respect

Jokic discussed the defenders who make his job difficult during an appearance on the Jao Mile podcast . When the conversation reached Gobert, the Denver star dismissed the idea that the Timberwolves center is overrated on defense.

"Rudy Gobert, I know people have all kinds of opinions about him, but Rudy is a good defender. He showed it in the last playoffs," Jokic said.

This praise means a lot , especially since Jokic still puts up big numbers against Gobert. Jokic isn't saying he can completely shut him down, but he is admitting that Gobert forces him to earn every single bucket.

The 2026 playoffs gave Jokic a fresh look at that challenge. Minnesota trusted Gobert to defend him without constant double teams, allowing the Timberwolves to keep their other defenders focused on Denver's shooters. The Wolves eventually eliminated the Nuggets in six games.

Gobert's biggest impact came when Minnesota stopped trying to hide the matchup. He took on Jokic directly and used his size to contest drives, absorb contact and challenge shots around the basket.

In Game 2, Jokic went 1-for-8 from the field when Gobert was his primary defender. He still finished with 24 points, 15 rebounds and 8 assists, showing why defending him is about limiting his comfort rather than expecting a complete shutdown.

That defensive approach also helped the Timberwolves protect the rest of the floor. Gobert could stay attached to Jokic while Minnesota's perimeter defenders stayed closer to Denver's shooters.

Jokic acknowledged that challenge again when discussing Gobert's work in the postseason. His praise came after a series in which Minnesota repeatedly trusted its center to handle one of the hardest defensive assignments in basketball.

Rudy Gobert Has A Different Kind Of Endorsement

Gobert has won four Defensive Player of the Year awards, but his playoff defense has remained a frequent topic of debate. That makes Jokic's comments especially useful because they come from the player who has had to solve that defense himself.

The Denver-Minnesota series did not turn Gobert into an unbeatable defender. Jokic averaged 25.8 points, 13.2 rebounds and 9.5 assists across the six games.

It did show what Gobert can do when Minnesota allows him to play to his strengths. He can occupy Jokic without constant help, giving his teammates the freedom to handle other threats.

That may be why Jokic's praise stands out. Gobert does not need to erase an offensive superstar from the box score to prove his value. Making that superstar work harder is part of the job, and Jokic has now said plainly that Gobert does it well.

articles.summary: The Saturday showdown between No. 4 Texas and No. 1 Ohio State has much more at stake than a win or loss. For Texas QB Arch Manning, it’s proving he’s NFL ma...
articles.body:
The Saturday showdown between No. 4 Texas and No. 1 Ohio State has much more at stake than a win or loss. For Texas QB Arch Manning , it's proving he's NFL material.

Ironically, nobody recognizes that more than the Buckeyes themselves.

On Friday, Ohio State coaches revealed the skills Manning brings to the field that they plan to watch for, per Bruce Feldman of The Athletic.

One defensive coach talked about the difference between him on film and how he was last year.

"He's fixed his throwing mechanics" he said.

Last year, Manning completed 17 out of 30 passes against Ohio in a 14-7 loss. He added one touchdown and threw one interception. The Ohio State defense stopped him in his tracks.

Additionally, a source close to the Longhorns revealed to The Athletic a critical update about Manning.

"He's cleaner — and he's way more confident now," the source said. "There's more talent around him. He was the team's best running threat last year."

articles.title: Falcons Name Cooper Rush Week 1 QB; Tua Tagovailoa Has Oblique Issue
articles.summary: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski announced that Cooper Rush will start at QB in Week 1, as Tua Tagovailoa deals with an oblique injury.
articles.body: We knew Michael Penix Jr. wouldn't be under center in Week 1 for the Atlanta Falcons. Apparently, neither will Tua Tagovailoa. Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski announced on Friday afternoon that Tagovailoa is dealing with an oblique injury and Cooper Rush will be the team's starting quarterback for their Week 1 road matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Jack Strand will be the backup quarterback. Tagovailoa, who's considered "week-to-week," per ESPN, appeared to suffer the oblique injury in practice on Thursday afternoon, with a video showing when he may have first felt the discomfort. Atlanta signed Tagovailoa, a 2023 Pro Bowler, to a one-year deal in March following his release from the Miami Dolphins. Last season (2025), Tagovailoa totaled 2,660 passing yards, 20 passing touchdowns, 15 interceptions and an 88.5 passer rating over 14 starts, while completing 67.7% of his passes. As for Atlanta's Week 1 starter, the 32-year-old Rush has 16 NFL starts under his belt, most recently making two starts for the Baltimore Ravens last season. He previously made 14 starts for the Dallas Cowboys (one in 2021, five in 2022 and eight in 2024). Meanwhile, Penix is recovering from a season-ending knee injury he suffered in Week 11 of last season and won't be on the active roster to open the year. Catch Rush and the Falcons in action against the Steelers on Sunday afternoon at 1 p.m. ET on FOX.

articles.body: En una jornada histórica en la sede del club antioqueño, James Rodríguez fue presentado oficialmente como nuevo jugador de Atlético Nacional, sellando su vínculo contractual hasta junio de 2027 y dejando impresiones contundentes sobre lo que significa vestir la camiseta verdolaga. Durante la rueda de prensa, el mediocampista cucuteño no escatimó elogios para su nuevo equipo y trazó una comparación que de inmediato retumbó en los medios internacionales. "Este club todos saben lo grande que es, es algo único. Le decía al presidente que lo que se veía desde fuera es el Real Madrid niño, es un club grande. Esta camiseta pesa mucho y me gusta sentir eso; sé lo que es jugar en estos clubes y estoy listo para lo que viene", afirmó el exjugador de la Casa Blanca. Rodríguez enfatizó que la decisión no fue difícil una vez sintió la conexión con el proyecto deportivo del director técnico Lucas González, con quien mantenía conversaciones previas. Tras una negociación fugaz de apenas tres días, el volante dejó claro que el reto de vestir la verde y blanca volvió a encender su ambición competitiva. Un elemento determinante en la llegada de James a Medellín fue el arraigo familiar. El mediocampista reveló que sus hijos son seguidores del equipo antioqueño y desempeñaron un papel clave en su toma de decisión final. En lo deportivo, el volante completó su primera práctica a la par del grupo y se encuentra bajo las órdenes de Lucas González. Aunque el número de su dorsal aún no se ha hecho oficial, el jugador manifestó que la cifra en la espalda no condicionará su entrega dentro del campo, manifestándose dispuesto a desempeñarse como volante creativo o extremo según las necesidades del esquema táctico.

articles.title: AC Milan Coach Reveals Christian Pulisic 'Upset' About Sitting On Bench
articles.summary: Christian Pulisic hasn't played for AC Milan yet, and is not happy about that fact.
articles.body: Christian Pulisic has not appeared in any of the three AC Milan games this season, and on Friday coach Ruben Amorim shared at a Friday press conference that the star forward is "upset" about that. While Pulisic has been listed as a substitute in each of the three games, he did not appear in them. The stated reason for the lack of playing time is recovery from a bone bruise and microfracture to his right tibia, which were revealed following the United States' exit from the 2026 FIFA World Cup. "He is angry because he has had zero minutes so far and I like that in my players," said Amorim, per GOAL. "Don’t forget that he had an injury in the summer and then in the first training session he took a knock and had to stop." Pulisic might not have to wait very long to finally appear in a game, however, as Amorim also shared that he is likely to play this weekend. "You will see him tomorrow, I don’t know whether from the start or during the game. I think he will play a few minutes." Amorim also revealed that just because Pulisic is a "name" does not mean that he gets to disrupt the current flow for AC Milan. "I will not take out those who are doing well just to put in a ‘name’: this is my way of managing the group and I will die with these principles," Amorim told assembled media. "Pulisic is very important for me. After the international break there are eight weeks with three games a week: everyone will be tired because of how much they will play. Pulisic is important and he will play a lot of matches. But you have to understand the context and my history to understand why I make certain choices. But you will see Pulisic from this weekend onwards." Christian Pulisic Related StoriesUp Or Down?
