The former player began his career managing in 2017, and is a two-time Primeira Liga manager of the year. Pulisic is in his fourth season with AC Milan, where he started in 32 and 29 games in his first two seasons, before playing in 30 games but starting just 18 in the 2025-2026 season.

articles.title: Jackson Martínez sale del retiro después de 6 años y firma con el DIM para enfrentar a James y Cuadrado
articles.standfirst: Jackson Martínez regresa al fútbol profesional: nuevo fichaje del Independiente Medellín para 2026
articles.summary: Jackson Martínez regresa al fútbol profesional: nuevo fichaje del Independiente Medellín para 2026
articles.body: En lo que ya se considera una de las ventanas de transferencias más llamativas de los últimos años, Jackson Martínez vuelve al fútbol profesional para vestir la camiseta de Independiente Medellín. El atacante chocoano de 39 años selló su acuerdo para unirse al Poderoso de la Montaña, firmando en principio por seis meses (hasta diciembre de 2026) con opción de extensión. De esta forma, el 'Cha cha cha' volverá a la actividad competitiva después de anunciar su retiro en 2020, para sumarse a la constelación de figuras repatriadas en la Liga BetPlay, donde se medirá cara a cara ante contrataciones rutilantes como James Rodríguez en Atlético Nacional y Juan Guillermo Cuadrado en Millonarios. Recientemente, a Jackson se le había visto activo compartiendo partidos de exhibición con figuras como Giovanni Moreno y el propio Juan Fernando Quintero. Sin embargo, pocos anticipaban que ese ritmo informal desencadenaría su regreso formal a la alta competencia. Con esta firma, el DIM suma una dupla de ataque con pasado tricolor y experiencia europea: Jackson Martínez volverá a tirar pared con Juan Fernando Quintero, quien ya venía sumando minutos en la plantilla dirigida por Luis Amaranto Perea. El movimiento actúa como un fuerte contrapeso del equipo del pueblo ante los recientes movimientos del mercado paisa y capitalino. Jackson Martínez dejó una huella importante en el balompié internacional. Tras consolidarse como el sucesor de Radamel Falcao García en clubes de élite como el Porto y el Atlético de Madrid, el delantero fue una pieza clave para la Selección Colombia en la memorable Copa del Mundo de Brasil 2014. No obstante, su trayectoria se vio seriamente afectada por una severa lesión en el tobillo izquierdo sufrida durante su estancia en la capital española. A pesar de someterse a múltiples tratamientos e intervenciones, la molestia limitó su continuidad durante su posterior paso por el Portimonense de Portugal, llevándolo a alejarse del fútbol profesional alrededor de 2020 a los 33 años. El destino del atacante vuelve al punto de partida. Martínez debutó profesionalmente con el Independiente Medellín en 2004 y permaneció en la institución hasta 2009, año en el que se coronó campeón del Torneo Finalización antes de emprender su travesía internacional hacia Jaguares de Chiapas en México. A sus 39 años y sintiéndose en plenitud física para asumir el reto, 'Cha cha cha' buscará repetir la gloria en el club que lo vio nacer, sumando jerarquía a un torneo que reúne a referentes históricos de la Selección Colombia.

articles.title: City boss Enzo Maresca says spotlight not on him ahead of Manchester derby
articles.summary: Maresca’s Man City lead the Premier League standings, with three wins out of three, ahead of Sunday’s derby.
articles.body:
Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca said he was not the “main focus” as he prepares to take charge of his first Manchester derby, seeking to maintain his team’s 100 percent record this season.

The City boss takes the Premier League leaders to Manchester United on Sunday in their toughest test of the season so far, after three successive wins in the top flight.

City have an impressive record at Old Trafford over the past 15 years, but lost last year in Pep Guardiola’s final game there .

Michael Carrick’s United have had a stuttering start to their season, winning just one of their opening three games to sit five points behind City.

Maresca, who previously worked as Guardiola’s assistant at City, said it was “very important” to get a first derby win this weekend, but stressed he had broader concerns.

“To be honest, I’m more thinking about the team, the fans, the table,” Maresca told reporters on Friday. “And for sure, if we win, it’s also good for me.

“But the main focus is not ‘It’s my first derby and I want to win the game.’ For sure, I want to win the game, but it’s because we want to continue to win games. That is good for everyone.”

City have been top dogs in Manchester since Alex Ferguson retired as a Premier League champion in 2013, finishing above them every season since.

Maresca said recent history was behind Elliot Anderson ‘s claim that City were the “kings of Manchester” after the midfielder completed his 116 million pound ($157m) move to the Etihad Stadium from Nottingham Forest.

“The reason why Elliot said that is because he grew up in the last 15 years,” said the Italian.

“I think Manchester City was unbelievable, what they achieved. So, I think it’s normal when Elliot said that.

“Then if you go back, it’s a different picture. But for me, the reason why Elliot said that is because when he grew up, Manchester City was dominant.”

articles.title: This Year's Breakout Star Will Be ... Tyler Shough? Why Scouts, Execs Like Saints QB
articles.summary: Who'll will be a breakout star in 2026? Execs and scouts pointed to Tyler Shough and a pair of Bears standouts.
articles.body: When we surveyed people around the NFL on which player could be the next Drake Maye or Jaxon Smith-Njigba and make a sudden leap in 2026, one common answer emerged. New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough was routinely mentioned by scouts and executives we spoke with as a rising star to watch this season. In fact, one NFL executive told us that there's no young quarterback "better set up for success" than Shough, while a scout told us that he was the best rookie quarterback last season. There were also a pair of Chicago Bears standouts that people around the league have their eyes on this season as rising stars. So, let's unpack what we're hearing about potential breakout candidates this season. Exec: ‘No Young QB Better Set Up For Success’ Ralph Vacchiano: Even the New Orleans Saints weren’t quite sure what they had in second-round quarterback Tyler Shough at the start of last season. But by the end of the year, it looked like they had found their quarterback of the future. He was also the best of the quarterback class of 2025, even though he made just nine starts. And some around the NFL think he should be even better in Year 2 since the Saints have surrounded him with a stellar supporting cast. "There is no young quarterback better set up for success than [Shough]," an NFL executive told me. "Kellen Moore is a brilliant offensive mind, for starters. And look what they surrounded him with. He already had [wide receiver Chris] Olave and [tight end Juwan] Johnson. And in the right hands, Travis Etienne is a terrific running back — way better than Alvin Kamara at this stage. "In a bad division, they could surprise some people. And his numbers could pop." Things would have looked even better for Shough if it wasn’t for the hamstring injury suffered by rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson, a player the executive told me "might be the best receiver in the draft." He’s out at least the first four weeks of the season, and he could be sidelined until mid-October, according to some reports. "That’s a blow for sure," one NFC scout told me. "But I think there’s still enough there for Shough to grow. Look at what he did last year. He’s got a much better team around him now." Scout: Shough Was Best Rookie QB In 2025 Vacchiano: The Saints were 6-11 last year, but that was enough to finish just two games out of first place (and the playoffs). Shough completed 67.6% of his passes for 2,384 yards, 10 touchdowns and six interceptions. He showed off a little mobility too (186 rushing yards, 3 touchdowns). "I don’t think there was a better rookie quarterback last year," the scout told me. "Maybe [Giants quarterback Jaxson] Dart will be better because he’s a real true dual-threat quarterback. But Shough has the ability to be an outstanding passer. And he’s certainly in the right hands." And as Shough showed promise toward the end of last season, the executive I spoke with expects him to take a step forward in 2026 now that he's spent a year in Moore's offense. "He was good at everything. But mostly he was poised and efficient and really ran that offense well without a lot of mistakes," the executive told me. "Moore will push him more this season, and I think he’s up to the task." Evaluator: Shough Already Made A Leap Last Season Eric D. Williams: Shough was a pleasant surprise for the Saints in the second half of the 2025 season, and talent evaluators I spoke with expect him to take another jump in his development in 2026. Shough, who was taken in the second round of last year's draft and was the third quarterback taken behind Cam Ward and Dart, lost the training camp battle with Spencer Rattler before becoming the starting quarterback for the final games. As Shough went 5-4 as a starter, one talent evaluator I spoke with noted one area he grew in as his rookie season progressed. "Shough took a large leap last year in the last quarter of the season handling pocket pressure," an NFL senior talent evaluator told me. "I think a full offseason with Kellen Moore will pay more dividends. A strong offensive line, nice receiving options and a proven offensive coach puts him in a great situation." A longtime NFL scout, meanwhile, noted that the 26-year-old's seven years in college should help him even more in 2026. "He is an experienced college QB who is coupled with a good player caller in the head coach," the scout told me. "He made a jump in the last part of the season, and I expect that to continue. The head coach will play to his strengths." Shough's Success No Surprise To His Coach At Louisville Williams: During Shough's final year in college, Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm got an up-close view of what his quarterback could do at the next level. In a collegiate career marred by injuries at Oregon and Texas Tech, Shough transferred to Louisville for his final college season, looking to reestablish himself as an NFL prospect. "For us, when we took him out of the portal, he wasn’t one of the hot names at all," Brohm told me. "He was somebody who had been injured and kind of gone through some ups and downs – been a starter, been benched – whether it was due to injury or whatever. And I think he wanted one last chance to show what he was made of. "It was a great fit. We wanted a guy who was hungry and wanted to make one year work. He wanted to prove he was durable. And when we researched it, when he got hurt a lot of times, it was because of designed runs. I told him we’re not going to do that; we’re going to run more of an NFL system here. We can work around that and get it to our running backs, and that’s what we did. He lasted all year." Louisville provided a dream scenario for Shough. He completed 63% of his passes for 3,195 yards, with 23 touchdowns and just six interceptions, leading the Cardinals to a 9-4 record. "He was durable," Brohm said. "He did a great job and played well in games. He was a good leader, had a good arm. He’s a natural leader and guys liked him. He was very approachable; he played hard and tough, and had grit. And when things didn’t go well, he didn’t point the finger at anybody. He just had a natural way to lead. He had really good qualities and intangibles that carried over to his talent and skill." Shough also helped his draft ascent at the combine, throwing the ball with zip during quarterback drills and running a 4.63-second, 40-yard time. Brohm said he wasn’t surprised by the success Shough had in his rookie season and expects him to have a solid NFL career. "I had a feeling that whoever took him was going to really like what they got," Brohm told me. "And I think that definitely showed through in the first year of his NFL career. He’s in a good system. It’s always great to start the year not as the starter, but as the backup. Which I thought was great because I knew maybe they wouldn’t perform well, and then when that happens midway through the year, everyone’s clamoring for him. And he stepped in and showed what he’s made of. So, I was very happy for him. He earned it and I think he’ll do great from here on." 2 Budding Stars To Watch For In Chicago Vacchiano: Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson has had a knack over the years of turning his offensive players into dangerous weapons. And he has two more in the pipeline in Chicago that might be ready to break out. An NFC scout told me that he thinks wide receiver Luther Burden III and tight end Colston Loveland are going to become "elite" players under Johnson’s guidance, and it could happen as early as this season — though that depends on how much Johnson features them in what could be a very diverse offensive attack. "I actually think Burden is going to end up as their No. 1 receiver ahead of Rome Odunze," the scout told me. "He’s got way better hands and is more reliable. Odunze is more explosive, probably, but at some point you lean on the guy who can make more plays. That’s Burden. He’s got great hands and strength. "And Loveland is right there with him. Johnson loves to rely on his tight ends too, so he’ll have plenty of opportunities. And you saw down the stretch last year what he can do with them." Loveland, the 10th overall pick in last year’s draft, did go off late last season after a very slow start. He caught just 11 passes for 116 yards in the first six games before he had his breakout. He was truly elite in his final four games, though — including two in the playoffs — when he had 28 catches for 378 yards and two touchdowns. Burden, meanwhile, put up only average numbers (47-652-2), but he also was only the target of 10.6% of Williams’ passes. Considering he caught 78.3% of the balls thrown his way, that target share surely will increase. "I’m telling you, Johnson is going to lean on those two," the scout said. "Let the defenses target Rome. Those are the two guys that will kill you."

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Royce Keys as World Champ, Oba Femi-Bronson Reed Interaction, Zilla Fatu's Future
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

WWE has reportedly been pleased with Royce Keys' work since forming the 946 stable with OTM a few weeks ago.

According to False Finish , Keys has received "massive praise" behind the scenes in WWE for assimilating well to a main event spot.

False Finish was also told by a source that "several higher-ups" in WWE view Keys as a potential future world champion.

After a solid run in AEW that saw him hold the TNT Championship and AEW World Trios Championships, Keys signed with WWE at the start of 2026.

Following a surprise appearance in the Royal Rumble, it took a while for Keys to gain a foothold on WWE programming, but he finally started to do it leading up to SummerSlam when he joined forces with LA Knight and Solo Sikoa to feud with The Bloodline.

Following an attack at the hands of Jacob Fatu, Keys returned a few weeks ago with a new attitude and with OTM in two.

Since then, Keys has done quality heel work in terms of his promos and his physicality, and it is starting to feel like he could be a major player in the company moving forward.

Important people in WWE apparently feel the same way, which bodes well for Keys' future prospects.

Reported Internal Reaction to Femi-Reed Interaction

Oba Femi shoving Bronson Reed's foot off of him during Monday night's episode of Raw reportedly elicited some strong reactions within WWE.

According to WrestleVotes on Fightful Select (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), the situation was not part of the script, and some in the company were not happy about how it played out.

Reed putting his foot on Femi following an attack seemed to be a callback to when Femi did the same to Brock Lesnar during their rivalry.

While Lesnar allowed it to happen and seemingly encouraged it, Oba took a swing at Reed's leg when he did it to him.

After missing months due to a torn biceps, Reed made his return to WWE programming last weekend at Sunday Night's Main Event during the match between Femi and Bron Breakker.

On Raw, Femi was taken out at the hands of The Vision, and Reed hit him with his Tsunami splash finisher multiple times.

As Reed and the rest of The Vision celebrated, Reed put his foot on Oba, only for The Ruler to show what appeared to be anger or frustration.

It is unclear if Femi was legitimately upset or merely attempting to make the angle look more authentic, but it got fans talking and speculating about a potential real-life beef between the Superstars.

Ultimately, that could prove to be a good thing since fans may be more invested when the eventual Femi vs. Reed match comes to fruition.

Zilla Call-Up Reportedly Expected in Near Future

Zilla Fatu has made an instant impact in NXT, but he may not be part of WWE's developmental brand for long.

Speaking this week on Wrestling Observer Radio (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Dave Meltzer expressed his belief that Fatu will get called up to the main roster "relatively soon."

Meltzer noted how over Fatu is with the NXT crowd, and pointed out that YouTube videos of Fatu's matches and segments have done numbers consistent with top stars like Cody Rhodes, CM Punk and Seth Rollins.

Fatu made his surprise WWE debut last month when he attacked Grayson Waller and Cruz Montana during a match to determine the No. 1 contender for the NXT Championship.

Then, in his first WWE match, Fatu was part of a Fatal 4-Way for the NXT Championship against Waller, Montana and Tony D'Angelo at Heatwave.

Although Fatu came out on the losing end, he bounced back with a win over Tristan Angels in his first NXT one-on-one bout.

As the son of late WWE star Umaga and part of the famous Anoa'i pro wrestling family, all signs point toward Fatu eventually having major involvement with The Bloodline when he makes it to the main roster.

Given that Solo Sikoa had a short stint in NXT before joining The Bloodline, it won't be a surprise if something similar happens with Zilla.

articles.title: Razaullah’s six-hitting debut caps Pakistan’s fightback against England
articles.summary: Pakistan all out with a second innings lead of 130 at the close on day three of the third Test at Edgbaston.
articles.body:
Debutant Razaullah launched a remarkable late salvo as Pakistan finally showed some fight on Friday to keep England waiting for a clean sweep in their three-Test series.

The fast bowler came to the crease with the tourists on the brink of defeat in the third Test at Edgbaston but clubbed nine sixes in an astonishing innings of 81 off 63 balls.

Fellow paceman Mohammad Abbas also joined the party as the pair took the score from 318-8 to 439-9, with England seemingly powerless to stop the carnage late on the third day.

It means the teams will have to come back on Saturday, with the home side needing to score 130 to wrap up a 3-0 win after dominating the series.

Earlier, Shan Masood scored 95 and captain Babar Azam made 76 as much-changed Pakistan passed 200 for the first time in the series at the sixth attempt.

Pakistan, facing a first-innings deficit of 320, lost two wickets without scoring a single run on Thursday, but opener Azan Awais and the experienced Masood took the score to 125.

Their partnership was broken in Friday’s morning session when Awais was caught down the leg side by stand-in wicketkeeper Jordan Cox off the bowling of spinner Dan Lawrence for 59, bringing Azam to the crease.

Masood was in sight of an eighth Test hundred when he fell to a sensational slip catch by Dan Lawrence off the bowling of Gus Atkinson.

Azam, who missed the first Test with an injured hand, batted fluently but got a feather of a touch to a Josh Tongue delivery, with Cox taking the catch.

Saud Shakeel (29) was next to go, caught by Emilio Gay at short leg while trying to fend off a Jofra Archer bouncer, while two more Cox catches accounted for Ghazi Ghori and Mohammad Imran.

But Pakistan were not finished as Abbas joined Razaullah at the crease for their show of evening fireworks.

Debutant paceman Razaullah showed his intent early, clubbing three sixes off Atkinson in four balls and the pair brought up their fifty partnership off just 57 balls.

Inspired, Abbas, with a previous top Test score of 29, smashed Ollie Robinson for six.

Razaullah reached an astonishing 50 off 43 balls with a fifth six, this time off Archer, repeating the dose the following ball to leave the England man shaking his head.

Abbas was eventually caught by Atkinson off the bowling of Tongue for 42, ending a partnership of 121 for the ninth wicket.

Razaullah had by now removed his helmet to face Lawrence, launching him into the stands to move into the 80s in the final over.

He survived an LBW on review but was stumped by Cox off the next ball for 81 as the spectators applauded him off.

In total he hit four fours and nine sixes to go with his four wickets in England’s first innings.

England bowled Pakistan out for a meagre 133 on the opening day before making 453 at a brisk pace.

Joe Root’s side have dominated the series, winning the first game by an innings and 103 runs and the second by 194 runs.

Pakistan released seven players and sacked head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant Umar Gul after their defeat in the second Test, making four changes to their side in Birmingham.

articles.title: Bears Reportedly Extend Starting RB D'Andre Swift On 3-Year Deal
articles.summary: The Chicago Bears have reportedly signed starting running back D'Andre Swift to a three-year extension.
articles.body: How Swift it is. The Chicago Bears have signed running back D'Andre Swift to a three-year, $33.75 million extension, ESPN reported on Friday afternoon. The deal includes $27.5 million guaranteed, with the $11.25 million average annual value putting Swift 14th among NFL running backs. Swift was entering the final season of a three-year, $24 million deal with the Bears. Last season (2025), Swift rushed for 1,087 yards and nine touchdowns on 4.9 yards per carry across 16 games, which were all career highs. He also reeled in 34 receptions for 299 yards and one touchdown. Swift and the second-year Kyle Monangai form a lethal, one-two running back punch in head coach Ben Johnson's offense. In what was his rookie season, Monangai rushed for 783 yards and five touchdowns on 4.6 yards per carry in 2025. In all, Chicago was third in the NFL with 144.5 rushing yards per contest last season. Swift, a 2023 Pro Bowler with the Philadelphia Eagles, has rushed for 1,023.0 yards and 7.5 touchdowns per season with the Bears from 2024-25, while also tallying 342.5 receiving yards per season over that span. The 27-year-old running back spent the first three seasons of his NFL career with the Detroit Lions (2020-22), who selected him with the No. 35 pick in the 2020 NFL Draft out of Georgia, before being traded to the Eagles for the 2023 season. Swift and the Bears open the 2026 regular season on the road against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday afternoon (1 p.m. ET on FOX).

articles.title: Lebrón y Augsburger se citan con los número uno en las semifinales del Paris Major
articles.standfirst: Tras salvar bola de partido en octavos, la dupla hispano-argentina avanzó a la penúltima ronda en Roland Garros, donde disputará el billete a la final frente a Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia
articles.summary: Tras salvar bola de partido en octavos, la dupla hispano-argentina avanzó a la penúltima ronda en Roland Garros, donde disputará el billete a la final frente a Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia
articles.body: La jornada de cuartos de final del Paris Major deparó cuatro compromisos de alto nivel competitivo en la pista Philippe Chatrier, con tres de los principales cabezas de serie resolviendo sus cruces para inscribir su nombre en las semifinales. Juan Lebrón y Leo Augsburger, que superaron una situación límite en la ronda previa, mostraron una versión sólida para certificar su clasificación. En esa misma rama avanza la pareja número uno del ranking, Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia, mientras que en la parte inferior del cuadro Alejandro Galán y Federico Chingotto, así como Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno, completaron el cuadro de semifinalistas. Lebrón y Augsburger venían de afrontar un punto de partido en contra en su duelo de octavos de final frente a Javier Barahona y Maxi Sánchez. Superado ese compromiso, la dupla hispano-argentina se midió en cuartos a Momo González y Lucas Campagnolo. Exhibiendo mayor fluidez en la construcción del juego sobre la moqueta parisina, Lebrón y Augsburger encarrilaron el encuentro tras llevarse el primer set por 6-3 y abrochar el pase a semifinales en un disputado tie-break en la segunda manga (7-6). En esa misma zona del cuadro, Arturo Coello y Agustín Tapia aseguraron su presencia en la penúltima ronda tras vencer a Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero por 6-2 y 7-5. Los líderes del ranking impusieron su ritmo en los compases iniciales y neutralizaron el empuje de sus rivales para sellar su clasificación sin necesidad de acudir al tercer set, citándose así de nuevo con Lebrón y Augsburger por una plaza en la gran final del domingo. En el otro lado del cuadro, Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto resolvieron su compromiso ante Aimar Goñi y Edu Alonso. La pareja revelación del torneo, que Venía de eliminar a Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas en la ronda previa, planteó una estrecha resistencia en el primer parcial, llevando la resolución al desempate. La veteranía de la dupla número dos decantó el tie-break a su favor (7-6), logrando posteriormente cerrar el billete a semifinales con un 6-2 en el segundo set. Por su parte, la plaza restante en semifinales se la adjudicaron Paquito Navarro y Martín Di Nenno tras remontar un choque de máxima exigencia ante Jon Sanz y Franco Stupaczuk. A pesar de ceder la primera manga por 4-6, el sevillano y el argentino reaccionaron con autoridad en el segundo parcial para igualar el choque con un contundente 6-1. En el set decisivo, Navarro y Di Nenno completaron la remontada por 6-4 para certificar su acceso a la penúltima ronda del Major parisino.

articles.title: DT Levi Onwuzurike cut by Detroit Lions, will he return to roster?
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions cut of Levi Onwuzurike follows the practice of NFL teams cutting vested veterans before Week 1 to avoid guaranteeing contracts.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions released defensive tackle Levi Onwuzurike on Friday, Sept. 11, two days before their season opener against the New Orleans Saints .

A second-round pick out of Washington in 2021, Onwuzurike was expected to play a rotational role on the Lions ' defensive line this fall and still could return on the 53-man roster next week or to the practice squad on Saturday.

NFL teams sometimes release veterans before the start of the regular season to avoid having their contracts guaranteed for the season. All vested veterans on Week 1 rosters have their salaries guaranteed.

The Lions would avoid guaranteeing Onwuzurike's salary by re-signing him to the practice squad, according to OverTheCap.com , but still could elevate him for Sunday's game.

The Lions also cut defensive tackle Tyre West from the practice squad Friday to open a practice squad roster spot.

Onwuzirke has a long injury history but was healthy in training camp. He missed all of last season with a torn ACL and did not play in 2022 because of a back injury.

Projecting 2026 Detroit Lions starters for Week 1 opener

The Lions went heavy on the defensive line when they set their initial 53-man roster, keeping 11 linemen. Alim McNeill and Tyleik Williams are expected to start at defensive tackle against the Saints, with Aidan Hutchinson at one edge spot and DJ Wonnum or Tyler Lacy starting at the other end position depending on the package.

Onwuzurike played both Lacy's big end spot and at tackle in the preseason.

Safety Christian Izien was the only Lions player with an injury designation for the Saints. He is questionable to play with a groin injury.

articles.title: Clarke Schmidt to make another rehab appearance Saturday, could rejoin Yankees after
articles.summary: Clarke Schmidt appears to be getting closer to finally returning to the Yankees.
articles.body:
The Yankees could be getting a nice boost in their bullpen soon.

Clarke Schmidt will make one more rehab appearance this weekend, Aaron Boone said pregame Friday.

The team will wait and see how that outing goes, but if Schmidt is able to get through it okay, then the skipper said a return during the next road trip could be in play.

Schmidt has thrown 5.2 innings through four appearances to this point.

He's been slowly building himself up to rejoin the club in a relief role after missing 400-plus days following the second Tommy John surgery of his career.

The righty hasn't pitched in a big-league game since last July.

Schmidt could be a nice weapon for the Yanks when he does return, though, as he's pitched to a 3.18 ERA out of the bullpen in his career.

Ryan Weathers could be joining Schmidt in that bullpen down the stretch, as well.

The left-hander is said to be doing extremely well during his throwing progression, and Boone said that it's possible he'll be able to return during the final week of the season.

He could make his way back onto the mound as soon as next week.

Weathers has been sidelined for just about three weeks now due to a left forearm flexor strain.

While there was initially some concern watching him leave his start, the expectation has been that he'll be able to help the Yanks again down the stretch in some capacity.

articles.title: "Toughest Competition Is Within Our Own Building"- JGR Driver Drops Revealing Truth on Intra-Team Friction at Joe Gibbs' Camp
articles.summary: Joe Gibbs Racing Toyotas have been the class of the field so far in the Cup Series. And with the start of the 2026 Chase for the Championship, they’ve contin...
articles.body:
Joe Gibbs Racing Toyotas have been the class of the field so far in the Cup Series. And with the start of the 2026 Chase for the Championship, they've continued that momentum. Christopher Bell clinched his first Southern 500 victory last Sunday, and he made big gains in the points standings. He trails Denny Hamlin by 12 points. With all four JGR drivers placed inside the top six in the Chase standings, it is clear that they are racing against their own teammates for the ultimate prize.

Now, this can become problematic, as all four teams would want to lift the Bill France Trophy. And in that process of competitiveness, the added pressure of racing against teammates can weigh on them. So, how is JGR dealing with the situation? Christopher Bell, speaking on SiriusXM Radio, didn't sugarcoat his feelings .

"It certainly does (get complicated), yeah, and we've had many conversations and we know that all four of us are going to have a great opportunity at this championship this year. So it's gonna come down to execution and limiting your mistakes. We've had some long talks on how we're going to treat each other. But I think we all know our toughest competition is within our own building."

Speaking of mistakes, a slow stop by the No. 11 pit crew after Stage 2 in Darlington put Hamlin back in traffic, leading into his tussle with Michael McDowell. He was fortunate enough to score 16 stage points, or Bell would've been leading the Chase standings. Chase Briscoe and the No. 19 team had a similar day after he ran out of gas in Stage 2 and gave up his track position.

Again, the good news was that Briscoe had enough time to bounce back for a sixth-place finish. As things stand, Briscoe is trailing Bell by 25 points, and Ty Gibbs is two points behind the No. 19 team. So, things are very tight, and given how close all the JGR cars have been running lately, there can be dramatic outcomes over the race win.

Last year, Denny Hamlin lost his cool against his own teammate, Ty Gibbs, at Loudon. They were both battling for 11th, and Hamlin, who was racing for the championship, didn't appreciate his teammate's hard racing. On Lap 110, while exiting Turn 4, Hamlin spun the No. 54 car and vented his frustrations over the team radio.

"Are they afraid to talk to him? That's what I feel like, they're just scared of him."

Ty Gibbs is the grandson of veteran team owner Joe Gibbs, and Hamlin felt that no one within the organization drew the lines on how the non-playoff drivers raced their teammates competing for the championship. So, there is history within the JGR camp of teammates turning on each other, and now that all four cars are in a position to win the title, this makes the situation even more sketchy.

Looking at the points standings, this title race is Joe Gibbs Racing's to lose. Hendrick Motorsports is struggling to find consistent speed and performance. Kyle Larson, who is arguably their best bet, is chasing a 49-point gap to leader Denny Hamlin. Joey Logano, placed eighth, has shown some speed recently, but he is expecting the leaders to fumble in order to capitalize.

Ryan Blaney is the only non-JGR driver who is matching their pace and sits third behind Hamlin and Bell. But again, the odds are stacked against him, as the JGR Toyotas have better speed across the board. Even Kevin Harvick was concerned about how the title is shaping up to be a team battle within the JGR camp.

"They just don't need to beat themselves up. Because in the end it's like you said earlier, one of them better win. Because in a year like this, when your cars are that, don't give it away by getting in a p****** contest with each other, that is not what you want to do. That will be embarrassing," Harvick said on the Happy Hour podcast.

Nine more races remain in the Chase, and it is going to be a test for the Joe Gibbs Racing drivers as they try to achieve their objective of winning the championship. For any non-JGR fans watching, they would be hoping for drama within this team, as that would allow other players to make this title run even more entertaining.

articles.title: Manchester United revokes 685 season tickets in touting investigation as fans plan demonstration
articles.summary: Manchester United have revoked 685 season tickets following the club's much-criticised touting investigation, with a demonstration by furious fans now schedu...
articles.body:
Manchester United have revoked 685 season tickets following an extensive and widely criticized probe into ticket touting at Old Trafford.

In August, the club flagged 1,617 accounts displaying "unusual activity." Those account holders were subsequently contacted and requested to explain the activity that raised red flags.

This aggressive tactic triggered fierce criticism from supporters , with many feeling that innocent and devoted fans were being unjustly targeted. A demonstration before Sunday's Manchester Derby at Old Trafford has been organized in response to what supporter group The 1958 described as penalties being imposed without "compelling evidence," as per The Mirror .

United have now revealed the outcome of their probe, which permitted fans to challenge decisions before an independent appeals panel. The club stated that 685 season tickets were withdrawn, including 499 for which a ban was confirmed by the appeals panel.

Meanwhile, 468 cases were settled after the season ticket holder supplied information clearing themselves. The club have acknowledged they "did not anticipate the extent" to which fans shared account details "in circumstances they regarded as legitimate," and in those instances no penalties were applied.

The club stated: "Bans were issued where there was significant misuse of the ticketing system for financial gain. This included the operation of organised ticketing networks, which were controlling, selling and distributing tickets from hundreds of accounts.

"These actions undermine fair access to tickets for genuine supporters and have no place at Manchester United.

"Our focus now turns to ensuring these tickets are returned to our supporters. All season tickets released through this process will be offered to supporters on the season ticket waiting list."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

The club added: "We want to allow any sanctioned ticket holder the opportunity to refer their case to the Independent Football Ombudsman. Therefore, we will wait until after the international break before reallocating season tickets.

"Any seats used on a match-by-match basis before then will be sold at season ticket prices, not matchday prices. The club is not profiting from this process."

The organization confirmed 226 accounts received final warnings for rule violations without financial motive, while 238 accounts found guilty of additional infractions had their original season ticket suspension reduced to a prohibition on home ticket forwarding and away match applications.

Prior to the club's Friday announcement, Chris Rumfitt, a spokesperson for Manchester United Supporters Trust (MUST), captured the discontent among supporters. He told Mirror Football : "If it was a clampdown on touting we would be entirely supportive, because the biggest losers of touting are fans who get exploited and ripped off.

"But what they are calling a clampdown on touting has brought up a huge numbers of match-going fans doing ordinary things match-going fans do, i.e. passing tickets between groups of friends at face value, which people wouldn't consider to be touting.

"There is no question that large number of ordinary fans have been caught up in this because what the club has defined as 'suspicious' included lots of things fans do."

Rumfitt contends that the issue has resonated so deeply with supporters that only the ill-fated attempt to establish a European Super League five years ago rivals the intensity of feeling among the fan base.

He added: "The approach the club has taken has been 'ban first, ask questions later.' They've banned people and then asked them to prove that they haven't done anything wrong, which isn't normally how things work in this country. The burden of proof works the other way around.

"There's a massive amount of discontent among all fan groups, it's really united the fans. The way the club has gone about this is completely wrong. It has spread further mistrust."

articles.title: Myles Garrett gets brutally honest about his disappointing Rams debut
articles.summary: It can be difficult to play an international game. Maybe that played into Myles Garrett's poor performance in Week 1.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett made his debut for the Los Angeles Rams in Week 1, but it didn't go quite as the franchise probably had hoped it would.

Just one year after setting the new NFL single-season sack record and winning Defensive Player of the Year honors, Garrett finds himself playing for the Rams after being traded from the Cleveland Browns . And his first game with the franchise could not have been more lackluster.

Garrett recorded zero sacks, zero tackles, and zero quarterback hurries as the Rams were beaten 27-7 by the San Francisco 49ers .

Myles Garrett struggles as Los Angeles Rams are defeated by San Francisco 49ers in Week 1

After the loss Garrett spoke with the media, and he certainly pulled no punches about how disappointed he was with his own performance, taking accountability for the poor effort and promising improvement.

"This was the worst version of myself I've put out there. I gotta be better," Garrett said.

There are plenty of possible reasons for Garrett's struggles to start the season. You could blame it on the travel itinerary , which saw the Rams travel to Australia on a 17-hour flight just one day before the game, not giving themselves time to acclimate to the time change. You could also blame growing pains as he adjusts to a new system and a new team.

But with all the hype surrounding the potential greatness of a defensive line anchored by the returning Aaron Donald (who did not make the trip for Week 1) and Garrett, the veteran defensive end will need to step up his game to live up to the insanely high expectations upon him this season.

According to Steelers Depot , Porter "tweaked his back during the team's mobility test" before the first training camp practice. He was activated from the PUP list during roster cutdowns and returned to practice Sept. 1.

Porter's contract situation also remains unresolved as he enters the final year of his rookie deal. The Steelers have made a formal offer, according to NFL Network's Mike Garafolo , but the two sides remain apart.

Porter said Friday he isn't optimistic about getting a deal done before Sunday's opener and pushed back on reports that he is seeking to become the NFL's highest-paid cornerback, calling those figures internet chatter.

articles.title: Cambridge United vs Reading: 2026/27 Match Preview
articles.summary: Can the Royals pick up a first away league win of the season in this trip to Cambridgeshire?
articles.body:
The Royals are thriving at the moment, playing some good football. Winning 3-1 against a tough Blackpool side was a statement, showing Reading can and will be up there this season.

Jack Marriott is on form too, with as Kyreece Lisbie and George Earthy also playing very well, and they are looking like a proper team again.

Cambridge United have also started strongly with two wins, two draws and one loss in their five games this season, with their most recent match being a 2-2 draw to Burton Albion.

They haven't scored many goals but haven't conceded many either, with most games ending something to one this season. They are however yet to keep a clean sheet, which is something they will like to work on.

Saturday, September 12 at 3pm will see the Cledara Abbey Stadium play host to the Royals. The stadium holds 10,847, with the weather looking nice at around 23 degrees.

Ollie Yates will be the referee. He averages five yellow cards and 23.3 fouls a game. The last time he refereed a game for Reading, he showed a whopping eight yellow cards.

In terms of head-to-head, the Royals are up three to one in recent years, with Reading actually beating Cambridge in their last three meetings, scoring at least three goals each time.

The last matchup saw ex-Cambridge attacker Harvey Knibbs score a brace alongside another ex-Cambridge player, Sam Smith, who grabbed the third in a 3-1 win. Current Royal Josh Stokes played in that game against Reading, so could be one to look out for against his former club.

In this preview I will look at the opposition and who can be important in the game, and I will give my predictions.

The hosts are a tricky side to play against, with their 3-4-2-1 formation solid defensively.

This year's stand-out player for the home side has been Ben Knight , scoring two goals and averaging a very respectable 7.07 rating from WhoScored in this season's games so far. Comparing him to other attacking midfielders this season, he is in the top 91% for goals and shot attempts.

Cambridge have conceded six goals this season, scoring seven in the process. They are yet to keep a clean sheet and, against a high-scoring Reading side, I doubt they will again in this one.

Cambridge aren't a possession-based team – they are more of a route-one counter-attacking side with their quick forwards running through gaps left in the defence.

In the previous game against Burton, they were 'out statted' in every aspect except touches in the opposition box, where they had more than double what the Brewers had (35 to 17).

Out of their three shots on target, they scored two of them, with Gassan Ahadme getting both. It was a late goal from Burton that saw the game end in a draw, but neither team looked like they deserved the victory.

Cambridge are hard to break down, but I think George Earthy can play a big part in this game. His off-the-ball forward runs are so important to the team, with him distracting players and pulling them out of position for Marriott to find the space. I think he will be the key to us breaking the deadlock.

I also see Jacob Brown once again coming off the bench to score late on.

Udoka Godwin-Malife, Paudie O'Connor, Benn Ward and Haydon Roberts will be the back line.

Lewis Wing and Andy Rinomhota will continue to play as the holding midfielders.

Kyreece Lisbie, Earthy and Daniel Kyerewaa will be the attacking three.

Marriott will be the lone striker up front.

We are deeply grateful to Kiesler Federal Credit Union for investing in our young people and supporting our mission to help every child reach their full potential as caring, responsible young adults."

articles.title: The Outlook - Week 1 (Page 4)
articles.summary: The Outlook is The Huddle's new matchups column. Kevin Tompkins will break down every fantasy-relevant player from each team every week.
articles.body:
Implied Point Total: Las Vegas 21.75, Miami 18.75

Willis' rushing ability gives him an easy bar to clear for top-10 fantasy quarterback production this season. Every quarterback who has rushed for at least 600 yards has finished as a top-10 fantasy passer, and almost three-quarters of those players have finished as a top-six fantasy passer. We're going to get a LOT of information right out of the gate on how Miami will operate its offense and how aggressive it will be with Willis at quarterback. Against one of the softer defenses in the NFL in Las Vegas, Willis has the chance to get off to a nice start in Week 1.

Fantasy Advice: Willis is a solid streaming option in Week 1 if you're daring enough, but the floor is pretty low. Even with a nice matchup, this may not be the week to play it cute at quarterback, since you likely drafted another quarterback ahead of Willis.

Not only is Achane one of the most efficient and explosive backs in the NFL, but he is also one of the best receiving backs in the NFL. No back in the NFL had more 10-plus-yard runs or 15-plus-MPH runs than Achane last year. In terms of the Dolphins and who stands to benefit in the post-Mike McDaniel era, it's really just Achane in terms of the high-end production. He's the focal point of the Dolphins' offense this season, and especially in Week 1 against the Raiders.

Fantasy Advice: Achane is a mainstay at the RB position on your roster. A must-start option against these Raiders, who were in the bottom half of the NFL in fantasy points allowed to running backs.

Coming out of UCLA in 2022, Dulcich always had the talent to be a deeper aDOT tight end that can bust seams and get downfield. His 12.7-yard aDOT in his rookie season with the Broncos showed a ton of receiving talent. However, injuries took their toll, and he bounced from Denver to the Giants, then landed with Miami in 2025. As a Dolphin last season, Dulcich was a small-sample demon, with 10.8 yards per target and a 2.31 YPRR on 31 targets and 145 total routes. Dulcich remains with the new Miami regime, where he'll have a real chance to stick past this season.

Fantasy Advice: Dulcich might be the most bankable non-Achane skill-position player for fantasy, but unless you're in tight end premium league and able to start multiple tight ends, Dulcich is best left on your bench in Week 1 against the Raiders.

After suffering an ankle injury that had everybody drafting Mike Washington Jr. in the seventh round for 18 hours, Jeanty has practiced in full the last two days and should be good to go for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Jeanty finished as RB11 after a solid but inefficient season in 2025. Averaging just 3.7 yards per carry last season, we should see some improvement in the offensive environment in 2026 under new head coach Klint Kubiak.

Fantasy Advice: In a primo matchup at home against the Dolphins, Jeanty is a solid RB1 and he should have a solid start to his 2026 in Week 1.

Well, Brock Bowers will be missing time as he's having his meniscus trimmed after getting banged up in training camp and preseason. What a time to be alive to have this news drop! (Thank you for waiting until 99% of drafts were in the books, Las Vegas!) Regardless, we must move on for now. In Week 1, Mayer will be next man up. He's no slouch as a second-round pick who was immediately usurped the second the words "Brock Bowers" came out of the lips of Roger Goodell at the NFL Draft podium a few years ago.

ANYWAY, Mayer is perfectly fine and very talented as a tight end; he just hasn't been featured too much outside of a Bowers injury. Earning a 21.2% TPRR last season on limited routes, Mayer has shown that he can earn targets when given the opportunity. For at least the first few weeks of the season, he'll get that opportunity.

Fantasy Advice: Mayer has thrived at times when Bowers has been out of the lineup, but with this opportunity against one of the worst teams at defending the tight end position in the Dolphins, I've got Mayer as a back-end TE1 and more than worthy of a start if you're more keen on him than your current tight end option. Mayer is an easy 1:1 pivot if you roster Bowers and don't already have another option. For those who roster guys like McBride, Warren, Kraft and that top-end group, there's not much need to go grab Mayer unless it's tight end premium or you have an empty bench spot and want to play some defense in your league.

Implied Point Total: LA Chargers 28.5, Arizona 19

During his stint as the Cardinals' starting quarterback last season, Brissett was QB8. His connections to Michael Wilson and Trey McBride fed families. Literally. Mine. It was glorious!

Anyway, back again is Brissett with a new head coach in Mike LaFleur. However, for a full season, can Brissett keep up that pace? It'll be tough with a lot of game tape around for defenses to study and stop the Cards' passing game.

Fantasy Advice: Against a tough Chargers defense in Week 1, this isn't the spot to unleash Brissett in 2026. I'm leaving him out of my fantasy lineups.

Jeremiyah Love is currently dealing with an ankle injury, but LaFleur is "optimistic" about Love's progress, even though the rookie's status for Week 1 is reportedly up in the air.

Love's sprained ankle suffered in the Cardinals' first preseason game has carried over into the first injury report of the season, but if he can play against the Chargers, we have to figure out whether he'll be part of a committee at the outset of the season with free-agent signee Tyler Allgeier . With James Conner on the PUP list to start the season, it's primarily a two-man backfield right now, with Bam Knight possibly spelling both for a carry or two.

Fantasy Advice: If Love misses Week 1, I have Allgeier as a flex play given the tough Chargers defense that allowed the second-fewest fantasy points to running backs and the likelihood that the Cardinals get down big. If Love DOES play, I have him as a flex play too, just on the pretty decent chance that he's still splitting work and rotating with Allgeier.

It's not as though Harrison has been BAD, but he's just not lived up to the lofty expectations placed upon him as the son of a Hall of Fame wide receiver. Missing five games last season, Harrison's numbers dipped across the board, but he'll continue to get every opportunity to shed that "bust" label that's honestly been a little unfair to place on him going into his third season as a pro.

Fantasy Advice: Facing the Chargers this week in the season opener, Harrison Jr. is a flex play that you're hoping gets some garbage-time opportunities if the Cardinals get down quickly.

From Week 11 through Week 18, Wilson had FIVE top-10 fantasy finishes and had just one game in his last eight with less than seven targets. To say Brissett was feeding him is a clear understatement. The question we're all asking this season about Wilson is if that second half is repeatable in 2026. With Brissett back and now Harrison and McBride, Wilson may find replicating that stretch a lot tougher.

Fantasy Advice: Allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points to opposing wide receivers, Wilson is a flex play at best against the vaunted Chargers defense.

It's hard to argue with McBride in your tight end slot. Posting 126 receptions for 1,239 yards and 11 touchdowns will certainly assuage one's doubts despite being on a bad Cardinals team. Having Brissett installed at quarterback for 2026 will help things in a new offense, and honestly, that's the best-case scenario right now for McBride's continued fantasy value. He had at least seven targets in every single game last season; if that's not consistency and production, I don't know what is.

Fantasy Advice: McBride is a must-start option at tight end each week he is active.

It feels like Herbert has been on the cusp of stardom for almost four seasons now but just can't quite get over the hump. In 2026, he has his best and most complete team around him, with his bookend tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt healthy, plenty of receivers and tight ends and stud running back Omarion Hampton . New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is joining the fray to tie it all together.

Fantasy Advice: With a cake matchup in Week 1 against the Cardinals, if you roster Herbert, you've got to start him this week.

The addition of McDaniel to what was a pass-centric offense under previous coordinator Greg Roman last season should lead this offense to become a bit more balanced in 2026. While Hampton was a large part of what the Chargers did on the ground – especially late in the 2025 season – getting more attempts and utilization under his belt will only help Hampton in his second season.

After missing a seven-game stretch in the middle of his rookie season, Hampton returned to action in Week 14 to average a solid 14.7 fantasy points per game from Week 14 through Week 17. As the bell-cow of this offense and a (mostly) healthy offensive line with bookend tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater, Hampton should take the next step to becoming a fantasy force in 2026 - especially with McDaniel calling plays.

Fantasy Advice: This feels like a launchpad game for Hampton, especially with Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) banged up and on the injury report this week. Hampton is an RB1 with a bullet in Week 1.

It's incredibly hard to ignore what we saw in McConkey's rookie season, but there are also reasons why McConkey's second season in 2025 wasn't as good as his first. Players like this don't just become bad all of the sudden. With a new play-caller and offensive coordinator in McDaniel, this Chargers' offense may be a bit more balanced in terms of run vs. pass. However, in terms of who is getting the ball, McConkey looks to be at the head of the pack when it comes to who can balloon his production in his third season.

Fantasy Advice: McConkey feels very good as a nice WR2 candidate who could blow up in a great matchup against the Cardinals. Allowing the seventh-most fantasy points to wide receivers last season, McConkey has a golden opportunity here at home in Week 1 to remove the landing gear and soar in his third season.

After a horrible first season in Los Angeles , Johnston has bounced back with two solid seasons, including his first top-36 fantasy season in 2025. As the prototypical X receiver, Johnston has taken the downfield role for the Chargers and been pretty successful with it, in contrast to players like McConkey, who run more short to intermediate routes.

Fantasy Advice: In a game that figures to be tilted towards the Chargers, Johnston is a worthwhile flex play against the Cardinals, who allow the seventh-most fantasy points to wide receivers.

Implied Point Total: Dallas 25.75, NY Giants 22.75

One of the best value quarterbacks in fantasy drafts this summer, Prescott finished as QB6 last season with 30 touchdown passes and over 4,500 yards. The rushing component of his game is nearly gone, but he's good for a couple of TD plunges a season and 100-200 yards. The Cowboys are going to score a lot and have CeeDee Lamb , George Pickens and Jake Ferguson to highlight the weaponry available to Prescott this season.

Fantasy Advice: With the Giants just a middle-of-the-road team in defensive EPA per pass attempt but allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to opposing signal-callers, we'll ride Prescott this week in a very solid matchup against the Giants.

Despite averaging just 3.6 and 3.7 yards per carry in 2023 and 2024 in his final two seasons as a Denver Bronco , the Cowboys signed Williams to a one-year deal in free agency last offseason. The hope was that Williams could find some of his pre-injury form. He found that and then some as he finished as RB12 on the season.

Among 48 qualified rushers last season, Williams was ninth in yards after contact per attempt, 11th in rush yards over expectation and was sixth in rushing expected points added (rush EPA). Not just that, but Williams also had his burst back with 26 runs of 10+ yards, which was good for 13th.

Fantasy Advice: Against the Giants, who traded away Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals , they could scuffle in the first week or two of the season. With the threat posed by Prescott, plus Lamb, Pickens and Ferguson, Williams is there to clean up. I like him as a high-end RB2 for fantasy in Week 1.

Lamb had a down season in 2025, having missed three games, but giving up a lot of touchdown equity to his teammate George Pickens. Still, you don't need me to tell you why Lamb should be in your lineup.

Fantasy Advice: If you roster Lamb, he's in your lineup.

George Pickens was unreal in fantasy football this past season, finishing as the WR5 in fantasy points per game. After trading for him last offseason, Pickens and Lamb have been a near-unbeatable wide receiver combination. With Lamb out for several weeks at the beginning of the season, Pickens put the Cowboys on his back in 2025 with five consecutive games with at least one touchdown. Pickens and Lamb both finished last season with massive efficiency, sporting a 2.35 and 2.37 YPRR, respectively. As the only player playing on the franchise tag this season, Pickens should be fine to continue his awesome production for the Cowboys.

Fantasy Advice: Pickens is a must-start option in a massively productive Cowboys' offense in Week 1. For me, he's a low-end WR1 with overall WR1 upside this week.

Ferguson is most definitely one of the most "eat your vegetables" tight ends you can roster in fantasy football, but he's in that Dallas Goedert "he's going to exist and be annoying for the wide receivers" role for the Cowboys. Let's not forget that Ferguson was fantasy's TE1 up until Week 8, when Trey McBride activated and went scorched earth on fantasy football. But quietly, Ferguson's always been a solid target earner, with targets per route run percentages at 20% or more in three of four seasons. Helping to buoy Ferguson's TE5 finish last season were his eight touchdowns, which could see a little scaling back. Ferguson will be plenty relevant this season, but doesn't carry the upside of the top-end names at the position.

Fantasy Advice: The Giants allowed the 12th-most fantasy points to the tight end position a season ago, but with the Cowboys' high-flying offense, I'm willing to give a little bump to Ferguson with all the defensive attention paid to Lamb and Pickens. For me, Ferguson is a low-end TE1 worthy of starting consideration.

The Giants' offense could be very good this year as long as health plays a factor, and Dart is at the forefront this season. With 487 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns on top of his 15 passing touchdowns, Dart was a per-game monster last season. Now getting a full season of Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers , plus some more depth like Malachi Fields , Darnell Mooney , Isaiah Likely and others, Dart is set up for success this season.

Fantasy Advice: Against the Cowboys in Week 1, Dart feels like a guy you just can't sit knowing he can create with his arm and his legs.

Skattebo's season was cut short in the middle of Week 8 against the Eagles with an ACL injury that ended his season. Averaging 20.5 opportunities (targets + carries) per game from Week 2 until Week 7, we saw Skattebo force the hand of then-head coach Brian Daboll. Under a new Giants regime with new head coach John Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Matt Nagy, Skattebo should get every opportunity to thrive in a productive system predicated around setting up the run and letting Dart create in and out of the pocket. And he's healthy – that we know of.

Fantasy Advice: Against a tough front featuring Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark , the Cowboys are a lot better against the run than against the pass. Still, Skattebo should see some work in the receiving game to establish a solid floor in addition to his work on the ground. He's a mid-range RB2 in Week 1.

Last season ended prematurely for Nabers as he tore his ACL and suffered meniscus damage as well. All is well, as Nabers has been practicing in full, and it's been confirmed that he's playing on Sunday Night Football against the Cowboys. Nabers' rookie season was sublime, with 165 targets, 109 receptions and 1,204 receiving yards. Nabers was on his way to besting those numbers when his injury hit in his fourth game of the season, but there's plenty of time to make that up this season and beyond for Nabers.

Fantasy Advice: If you're rostering Nabers, you have to start him this week against the Cowboys on Sunday night.

Can Likely rise above the non-Nabers riff-raff in the Giants' receiving room to be the second target? All we've seen from Likely are small samples, but coming over from Baltimore in free agency to reunite with Harbaugh, Likely has a solid shot to get a full-time role at tight end and be a difference maker alongside Nabers. Likely has shown some moderate efficiency, but had his worst season as a pro last season with just a 14.3% targets per route run and 1.29 yards per route run. A season with over 60 targets for Likely will be his first, and it's probably going to happen this season. Will any efficiency come with it?

Fantasy Advice: The Cowboys were a middle-of-the-pack defense last season against fantasy tight ends, so it's probably a wash for Likely on an offense that also figures to be in the middle of the pack. He's a high-end TE2, but I'm not going out of my way to start him in Week 1 unless we see some gaudy target numbers and high-end utilization right away.

Denver Broncos at Kansas City Chiefs – 8:15 PM ET

Implied Point Total: Kansas City 23, Denver 20.5

The Broncos added Jaylen Waddle to the Denver mix via trade and added him to Courtland Sutton , Marvin Mims , Pat Bryant , Evan Engram and Troy Franklin . Nix is certainly not without passing-game weapons. First-time play-caller and offensive coordinator Davis Webb was given the keys to the offense by head coach Sean Payton and should be able to cook with this recipe in 2026.

While it could be a little different Broncos offense than we've been accustomed to, a more modern iteration of it could unlock even more potential with pre-snap motion and the hope of a more condensed personnel utilization than we've been used to with Payton over the last two decades-plus. Nix is coming off back-to-back fantasy QB7 finishes to start his career. A trip to Kansas City, as tough as it may be, could actually be a good thing this early.

Fantasy Advice: Nix will be working against a completely remade Kansas City secondary with rookie corner Mansoor Delane, plus the returning L'Jarius Sneed and safety Alohi Gilman . With Chamarri Connor also unlikely to play, it opens things up for Nix. I like him as a low-end starter this week, where Nix can unleash Waddle, Sutton and the rest of the offense without a lot of resistance.

RBs R.J. Harvey, J.K. Dobbins, & Jonah Coleman

Harvey ramped up his production in the back half of last season, and it's still a muddy backfield with no answers. Not great! Dobbins thrived last season in what was basically an every-down role for Denver before a Lisfranc injury put him out for the season after Week 10. He was brought back in free agency to continue handling that early-down role for the team and working in tandem with Harvey.

Now, Coleman enters the chat and it's even muddier. Drafted in the fourth round, he offers a bit of a varied profile, taking parts from both Harvey and Dobbins' skill sets. It's hard to know how this backfield shakes out in Week 1, but we'll get some answers at the very least.

Fantasy Advice: At the outset, I'm fine starting both Harvey and Dobbins as low-end flex plays, and keeping Coleman being on the bench until we get a true sense of what roles each player has and how it will shake out.

Traded to Denver in the offseason, Waddle has been one of the most efficient per-route receivers in the NFL over his five seasons in Miami, and he still commands targets at an excellent rate with 23.8% targets per route run last season. We know Denver will score quite a bit, and Nix can let Waddle work the middle of the field to great success. If Webb can keep the big route numbers to Waddle and Sutton, while rotating the other wide receivers like Bryant, Franklin, Mims and others amongst each other and not the top receivers, we'll be cooking with gas. Week 1 will be a big test and showcase for Webb, as he, Waddle and the rest of the Broncos face the Chiefs and a remade secondary.

Fantasy Advice: Waddle should be in every lineup as a locked-in WR2 with upside for much more on Monday Night Football.

Sutton may be entering his age-31 season, but we'll see if he continues to produce for the Broncos in 2026. Denver traded for Waddle during the offseason, and he is likely the top receiver now for the Broncos. With new offensive coordinator Davis Webb taking the play-calling reins from Sean Payton, this offense could get a little more concentrated and certainly a bit more modern in its approach. With that said, Sutton is fine for what he is: a professional receiver.

Fantasy Advice: Facing off against Kansas City, Sutton may get some nods in the flex from fantasy managers who are looking for immediate production. I don't even hate him as a WR3, either.

Expecting to play in Week 1 with no limitations, Mahomes rehabbed his left knee after a torn ACL and LCL ended his season last December. Prior to that injury, he was on pace for over 500 rushing yards and looking to have his best fantasy season since his QB1 overall finish in 2022. A Mahomes without limitations is scary for multiple reasons, but good news for anybody rostering his pass-catchers.

Fantasy Advice: Starting Mahomes in fantasy feels a bit scary, but I'd be willing to do it if I didn't have another backup or another capable quarterback on my roster. That IS a tough Broncos defense he's going up against, even at home in the friendly confines of Arrowhead.

It's difficult to imagine that Walker wouldn't be a monumental improvement to the Chiefs' running game and offense. Leaning on Walker would be wise for the Chiefs, who will likely have Mahomes back in the saddle at quarterback less than a year after a torn ACL. It's also fair to question if Walker will be as effective as he was in last season's playoffs and Super Bowl, now that he got his huge free-agent contract. With that said, Walker should be a big-time bell-cow for the Chiefs against a stout Broncos' front that allowed the fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs last season.

Fantasy Advice: Walker is a low-end RB1 or high-end RB2 in Week 1 against the Broncos, and should get a sizable workload on Monday night.

When on the field, Rice is a target-earning machine at a super low aDOT. Key phrase: "on the field." Rice has played in just 12 of a possible 34 games over the last two seasons because of suspension and injury, so it's certainly been an odyssey rostering Rice. With that said, he's practicing in full and should be good to go as the Chiefs are at full strength with Mahomes back in the fold for Week 1.

Fantasy Advice: Rice, as long as he's healthy, is a must-start fantasy option.

While we want to write off Worthy as "another Mecole Hardman Jr.-like bust", Worthy is entering his third season and still has the touchdown equity from being on the Chiefs and in an offense tied to Mahomes; we do need to see more to really buy in. Luckily, his price on draft day was nice, but we need actual on-field production.

Fantasy Advice: In a tough matchup against the Broncos, I'm keeping Worthy on my bench with the hope that he figures it out in his third season. He's one of the best bench holds, but the information we'll get in the first week or two of the season will tell us if we need to keep holding on to him or not.

For fantasy football, Kelce has been a model of consistency throughout his long and storied NFL career, with 10 straight seasons of at least 100 targets and never finishing worse than TE7 at any point in his career. Up until last season, Kelce had a TPRR above 20% in every season. Kelce's PPR value holds even more weight, with no fewer than 72 catches and 823 yards in his 11 seasons after his first full season in 2014. He still maintained a solid 8.3 yards per target last season, fully in line with his prime marks, as well as a 20% first-read target rate.

This season, Kelce is a more projectable volume fantasy play than an upside, ceiling play. He's still going to get his receptions, but some of the YAC stuff may keep falling due to the ravages of age. Father Time comes for everybody, after all. Week 1 is going to be especially tough, even at home, against the Broncos, who are a big-time AFC contender. They allowed the eighth-fewest fantasy points to tight ends last season, so they can make life tough for an on-the-mend Mahomes and Kelce in his advanced age.

Fantasy Advice: Kelce is a perfectly fine TE1 in Week 1 even against the Broncos' tough defense, but especially in PPR formats where he can rack up catches.

articles.title: Raiders final Week 1 injury report: Status of Ashton Jeanty, Brock Bowers

With Ashton Jeanty a full participant all week and no setbacks from the ankle injury he suffered in training camp, he has been removed from the Raiders injury report for their season opener against the Miami Dolphins .

Brock Bowers has been ruled OUT for the game. The former All Pro tight end had a procedure done to trim his meniscus this week which meant he would miss the season opener and possible additional games as he recovers.

With Bowers not playing, the starting tight end for Las Vegas will be Michael Mayer with Ian Thomas as the backup. As Bowers was expected to be the top target in this offense, the Raiders ' wide receiver corps will have to step up. Most notably Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor , and Jack Bech .

articles.title: Bears running back D'Andre Swift agrees to 3-year contract extension
articles.summary: Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift has agreed to a $33.75 million, three-year extension.  Swift's agency, Athletes First, announced the contract on Ins...
articles.body:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. (AP) — Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift has agreed to a $33.75 million, three-year extension.

Swift's agency, Athletes First, announced the contract on Instagram on Friday. ESPN reported that the agreement includes $27.5 million in guaranteed money.

The Bears visit the Carolina Panthers for their season opener on Sunday.

Swift, who turns 28 in January, rushed for a career-high 1,087 yards and nine touchdowns last season. He also caught 34 passes for 299 yards and a TD.

Led by Swift and Kyle Monangai , Chicago finished third in the NFL with 2,456 yards rushing in Ben Johnson's first year as coach. Monangai rushed for 783 yards and five TDs in a surprising rookie season after being drafted in the seventh round.

Swift joined Chicago in March 2024 , agreeing to a $24 million, three-year deal in free agency.

Swift was selected by Detroit in the second round of the 2020 draft. He spent his first three seasons with the Lions, rushing for 1,680 yards and 18 TDs.

He was traded to Philadelphia in April 2023. He made the Pro Bowl in his lone season with the Eagles , rushing for 1,049 yards and five touchdowns on 229 carries.

articles.title: Myles Garrett Bashes His Play in First Game for Rams: ‘The Worst Version of Myself’
articles.summary: The NFL’s reigning Defensive Player of the Year finished the game against the 49ers without a tackle — for the first time since 2024
articles.body:
Myles Garrett was candid about his Los Angeles Rams debut

"I wasn't who I needed to be for my team," he told reporters after the team lost to the 49ers , 27-7

Garrett has been struggling with swelling in his knee

Myles Garrett is focused on "getting healthy" after a disappointing debut with the Los Angeles Rams.

The star linebacker, who set the NFL record for single-season sacks last year when he was with the Cleveland Browns , finished the game against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, Sept. 10 in Australia without a tackle — and he acknowledged that he's "got to be better," while dealing with swelling in his knee.

"When I was out there, I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed," Garrett, 30, told reporters after the Rams' 27-7 loss. "I wasn't who I needed to be for my team."

The Texas A&M standout added that he was "the worst version of myself that I've put out there," and said his knee was not 100% healthy going into the game.

According to ESPN, Garrett told head coach Sean McVay that he was "feeling about 85%" during training camp, where he was seen wearing a brace on his left leg.

The last time Garrett went without a single tackle was in Week 11 of the 2024 season, and it has happened just four times in his career.

Any loss of mobility on Garrett's part was lost on the Niners.

"He's one of those players where it's just, you know, no matter what he's going through, it's still not an easy out for anybody," San Francisco left tackle Trent Williams said.

For the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, the bar is high.

"I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before," Garrett said.
