articles.title: Cowboys and Saints are perfect trade partners after Malik Davis injury
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have lost Malik Davis to an injury and they should consider calling the New Orleans Saints about a trade for a replacement.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have a new injury in their running backs room that could have them looking for an addition that the New Orleans Saints might be able to provide.

According to Cowboys co-owner Stephen Jones, Malik Davis suffered a hip injury at practice on Friday that is expected to keep him out long term.

"I think we're looking at a pretty serious injury that could take him out for some period of time," Jones said of Davis on 105.3 The Fan . "We don't have the final details. We'll know more (soon)."

Davis was the Cowboys' No. 2 running back behind Javonte Williams and his injury now leaves Dallas with only one other true running back on the roster outside of Williams, which is Emari Demercado .

The Cowboys will likely add another back at some point, but how they go about that remains to be seen.

Cowboys, Saints are perfect trade partners

The Saints are a team that has strong depth at the running back position .

After signing Travis Etienne to a big deal in free agency, that pushed Alvin Kamara , Kendre Miller and Audric Estime further down the depth chart.

There was uncertainty surrounding Kamara's future with the team all offseason long before the two sides agreed to a re-worked deal to keep the veteran in town.

The Saints might be willing to deal Kamara if a team like the Cowboys comes calling. Miller, who is in the final year of his rookie deal, is another possibility.

Kamara isn't the player he once was, but he can still make an impact as a runner and pass-catcher, and he's adequate in pass protection.

Miller's powerful running style is closer to what the Cowboys have in Davis, but he is far less proven than Kamara and is shaky in pass protection.

Kamara would easily be the more exciting addition for Dallas, but he might be too important to the Saints for them to trade him. Miller is a more realistic option for the Cowboys and would cost less.

articles.title: Why a Zach Neto trade by Angels could be a bad sign for 2027 season
articles.summary: If Zach Neto is traded, the 2027 season could be a huge letdown.
articles.body:
For the first time in a very long time, there is some optimism about the future of the Los Angeles Angels . It's all thanks to Arte Moreno selling the team and John Mozeliak selling off a few of their controllable pieces at the trade deadline.

Looking ahead to the 2026-2027 MLB offseason, the Angels could be looking to make even more trades, with Zach Neto 's name likely one of the top ones to watch.

However, if the Angels trade Neto, it could be a sign of bad things to come in 2026. As MLB.com's Mark Feinsand highlighted in a hypothetical Neto trade, it could come in the wake of a new general manager eyeing a complete teardown.

Why a Zach Neto trade could lead to a roster teardown

"With three more years of arbitration eligibility remaining, Neto would be the Angels' most attractive trade chip if the new general manager - whoever that may be - wants to tear the roster down and start their own rebuild," Feinsand writes.

This Angels team isn't good right now; there's no denying that. Mike Trout is nearing the end of his career, and the depth of this roster is bleak.

However, if the Angels were to enter a complete roster teardown and rebuild, it would make the 2027 season, and maybe a few more years afterwards, into majorly disappointing seasons.

The Angels have been stuck in mediocrity at best for a while now, and getting back to an above .500 record as soon as possible is ideal.

Trading Neto would land a haul and help the team in the long-term, but it would set them back for the next couple of seasons at the big-league level.

Essentially, it'd all but guarantee that Trout won't return to the playoffs unless the Angels were to trade him elsewhere. He has been linked to the Philadelphia Phillies plenty during his career, but he has shown no intention of asking for a trade.

Even if it's not the most productive endeavor, the Angels should try to compete with Trout's last remaining seasons on the roster.

Neto is a key player in such a plan, and trading him away would likely end any chance this team has at competing for the next few seasons, which are likely to be Trout's last years as a productive ballplayer.

Sure, the Angels might be looking to rebuild this team with a new owner and new general manager. But selling Neto and beginning a major roster teardown would be a huge disappointment for Trout and the Angels for the next few seasons.

articles.title: Three Tests, six innings, 20 runs: Pakistan openers register worst Test series in 35 years against England
articles.summary: In a dismal display, Pakistan's opening batsmen faltered throughout their recent Test series against England, accumulating a mere twenty runs across six part...
articles.body:
Pakistan's opening batters endured a disastrous Test series against England, combining for just 20 runs across six opening partnerships in the three-match series, their joint-worst performance in 35 years. The latest failure came in the third Test at Edgbaston, where Pakistan's opening pair was dismissed without adding a run to the scoreboard in the second innings. The 20-run aggregate is Pakistan's lowest for an opening partnership across a Test series since their home series against the West Indies in 1990-91.

Three opening combinations, no 10-run stand

Pakistan tried three different opening combinations during the series, but none managed to produce even a double-digit stand.

Across six innings, Pakistan's openers managed just 20 runs, with their best opening stand being only eight runs.

Azan Awais was the only Pakistan opener to offer any consistency during the series. The youngster scored 129 runs in six innings at an average of 21.50, but received almost no support from his partners. Imam-ul-Haq managed scores of 42 and 0, Shan Masood made 1 and 26, while Saim Ayub returned 0 and 0 in his two innings as an opener. The repeated early dismissals left Pakistan's middle order under pressure almost immediately.

Pakistan's problems at the top were part of a much wider batting collapse in the third Test. In the first innings at Edgbaston, Pakistan were bowled out for just 133, with their top five batters all dismissed for single-digit scores. It was the first time a team had lost all of its top five wickets for single-digit scores in the first innings of a Test in England.

articles.title: Super League: Wigan Warriors storm to League Leaders' Shield success with win vs Catalans Dragons and remain on treble course
articles.summary: Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley, Adam Keighran score as Wigan demolish Catalans to win League Leaders' Shield; Super League play-offs on September 18, live on Sky Sports, with Grand Final on October 3
articles.body:
Having clinched Challenge Cup glory in May at Wembley with victory over Hull KR, Wigan lifted their second piece of silverware on Friday via a dominant home success over the Dragons.

Warriors scored nine tries through Harry Smith, Liam Marshall (two), Brad O'Neill, the retiring Liam Farrell, Austin Daniel, Jai Field, Zach Eckersley and Adam Keighran. Keighran also added 14 points off the kicking tee.

The only other side capable of claiming top spot and the League Leaders' Shield had been Leeds Rhinos, and owing to their far greater points difference, a victory over Hull FC would have been enough had Wigan slipped up, but Peet's side ensured that was never likely to happen. In any case, Leeds fell to a shock 18-12 home defeat to Hull on Friday.

Wigan will now seek to finish their season by clinching a treble with Super League Grand Final success at Old Trafford on October 3, having suffered final defeat last season to Hull KR.
